The postoperative course was uneventful, and follow-up echocardiography at six months confirmed satisfactory prosthetic valve function without complications.
This case illustrates that tricuspid valve replacement can be safely and effectively performed in patients with ccTGA complicated by dextrocardia and situs inversus totalis. A left-sided surgical approach, combined with thorough preoperative imaging and careful intraoperative anatomical verification, may help restore operative orientation and reduce technical complexity in patients with mirror-image cardiac anatomy.

title: Determinants of outcome in atrial functional tricuspid regurgitation.
authors: Jawza Aldakhil; Kush Patel; Sveeta Badiani; Steffen E Petersen; Guy Lloyd; Sanjeev Bhattacharyya
abstract:
Atrial functional tricuspid regurgitation (AFTR) is increasingly recognized as a result of atrial remodelling in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). However, prognostic predictors in this population remain incompletely defined.
To evaluate echocardiographic characteristics and identify predictors of all-cause mortality in patients with AFTR.
We retrospectively studied consecutive patients with AF who underwent transthoracic echocardiography between 2017 and 2025. Inclusion required significant right atrial remodelling, defined as a right atrial area > 25 cm2. Patients with at least moderate functional tricuspid regurgitation comprised the AFTR cohort, while patients with mild/trivial/no tricuspid regurgitation served as controls. Patients with primary valvular disease, cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease, device-related valve disease, RV dilatation, or more than mild RV systolic dysfunction were excluded. Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to identify predictors of mortality.
A total of 152 patients were included, comprising 120 patients with AFTR and 32 controls. Compared with controls, patients with AFTR demonstrated larger atrial dimensions, higher right-sided hemodynamic-burden, impaired RV longitudinal strain, and reduced reservoir RA strain. During a median follow-up of 6.3 years, 53 deaths (45%) occurred among patients with AFTR. In univariable Cox analysis, age (HR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00-1.04; p = 0.016), TR Vmax (HR 1.59, 95% CI 1.07-2.35; p = 0.020), and lower reservoir RA strain (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.84-0.96; p = 0.003) were associated with mortality. In multivariable analysis, reservoir RA strain remained independently associated with mortality (adjusted HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.81-0.95; p < 0.001).
AFTR is characterized by marked biatrial remodelling and impaired right atrial function. Reduced RA reservoir strain was independently associated with mortality, supporting a potential role for RA deformation imaging in risk stratification in AFTR.

title: Late cardiopulmonary morbidity in patients with Hodgkin lymphoma: a retrospective nationwide registry study.
authors: Noora Hannuksela; Outi Kuittinen; Aino Rönkä; Anna Anttalainen; Liisa Ukkola-Vuoti; Iiro Toppila; Johanna Vikkula; Jan Seppälä; Kristiina Vuolukka; Katja Marin; Hanne Kuitunen; Tatu Miettinen; Anu Partanen
abstract: Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) is a B-cell neoplasm with a cure rate of 90%. Previous data on late morbidity in patients with HL cover the era of older treatment modalities. This real-world study consisted of 2912 patients diagnosed with HL between 2000 and 2019 in Finland and aimed to clarify the incidence of late-onset cardiopulmonary morbidity compared to matched controls. Patient data were collected from four nationwide Finnish healthcare registries. We reported a higher occurrence of coronary artery disease in patients aged < 50 years at diagnosis than in controls (RR 3.80 (2.16-6.74), p < 0001). Additionally, a higher incidence of both heart failure (RR 1.68 (1.28-2.21), p < 0.001) and valvular heart disease (RR 1.80 (1.17-2.78), p = 0.006) was detected in patients aged ≥ 50 years at diagnosis than in the controls. Remarkably, in the < 50 years age group, the incidences of pneumonia (RR 4.89 (3.58-6.71), p < 0.001) and pulmonary embolism (RR 7.78 (2.75-21.95), p < 0.001) were higher than those in the control group. In conclusion, with the current treatment modalities, late cardiopulmonary morbidity in long-term survivors remains a great challenge. A strategy for primary prevention and early detection of late toxicity remains crucial and a critical evaluation of current treatment practices is warranted.

title: Investigating Factors Associated with the Occurrence of Atrial Fibrillation after Non-cardiothoracic Surgery.
authors: Alireza Nematollahi; Parvin Bahrami; Mahshid Farshidnejad
abstract:
Although the occurrence of atrial fibrillation (AF) after cardiac and thoracic surgery is common and leads to serious complications such as patients' vital organ dysfunction, pulmonary edema, myocardial infarction, and death, evidence about the occurrence and risk factors associated with post-operative atrial fibrillation (POAF) as new AF immediately after non-cardiac thoracic surgery is limited. Therefore, the present study aimed at investigating the factors related to the occurrence of POAF after non-cardiothoracic surgery.
The present retrospective study was conducted on 272 patients undergoing non-cardiothoracic surgeries during 2007-2020. Patients' basic and clinical information including age, sex, BMI, addiction, comorbidities, history of non-cardiac thoracic surgery, history of cardiac surgery, history of chronic kidney disease (CKD), history of ischemic heart disease (IHD), history of heart failure (HF), valvular heart disease (VHD), and the occurrence or non-occurrence of POAF was extracted from their records and then documented.
In the present study, 48.1% and 51.9% of patients were with and without POAF, respectively. Risk factors associated with increasing the odds of POAF occurrence included age (OR = 1.094), anemia (OR = 3.947), IHD (OR = 4.23), CKD (OR = 4.765), VHD (OR = 4.781), pulmonary diseases (OR = 7.828), hypertension (HTN) (OR = 8.336), HF (OR = 11.790), and post-thoracic surgery (OR = 49.072) (P-value < 0.05).
According to the results of the present study, aging, comorbidities (i.e., anemia, pulmonary diseases, HTN, and CKD), heart diseases (i.e., IHD, VHD, and HF), and post-thoracic surgery were among the most significant risk factors associated with the increased occurrence of POAF.

title: Rheumatic lesions of the pulmonary valve: A systematic review of the literature.
authors: Martin Wendlassida Nacanabo; Anna Tall-Thiam; André Arthur Taryètba Seghda; Ella Hatoula Lengani; Prisca Lamoudi Thiombiano; Claudine Djième Dah; Mureille Loya-Abouga; Aimé Arsène Yaméogo; Adolphe Benjamin Ouattara-Zingé; Georges Christian Rosario Millogo; Jonas Koudougou Kologo; Yibar Kambiré; Valentin Nobila Yaméogo; André Koudnoaga Samadoulougou; Patrice Zabsonré
abstract:
Rheumatic pulmonary valve disease accounts for<1% of cases of rheumatic heart disease. Because of its rarity, this valvular disease is often overlooked and underdiagnosed.
To conduct a systematic review of reported cases of rheumatic pulmonary valve disease worldwide.
Studies reporting confirmed cases of rheumatic pulmonary valve disease, and providing sufficient clinical, diagnostic, therapeutic or follow-up data were included. Duplicate checking, selection, data extraction and quality assessment of the included studies were carried out by two reviewers, independently. The Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools were used for quality assessment. The process did not result in a meta-analysis because of significant heterogeneity and a lack of data. The review protocol is registered on the Prospective Registry of Systematic Reviews (CRD420261341732).
We identified 909 publications across the six databases. Following deduplication and selection, we included a total of 30 studies involving 35 patients, published between 1931 and 2025. Case reports predominated, accounting for 87% of studies (n=26); case series accounted for 13% (n=4). Age ranged from 3 to 83 years (median 29 years). There was a female predominance (n=20; 57%). India accounted for 37% of cases (n=13), followed by the USA with 11% (n=4). Only 46% of patients (n=16) presented with acute rheumatic fever or pre-existing rheumatic heart disease on admission. Dyspnoea was a constant symptom in all patients. Seven patients (20%) presented with atrial fibrillation. A procedure was performed in 74% of cases (n=26): pulmonary valve replacement in 40% (n=14); balloon dilation in 11% (n=4); and intraoperative commissurotomy in 20% (n=7). The clinical outcome was favourable in 74% of the documented cases (n=26).
Rheumatic pulmonary valve disease is a rare condition, but is likely to be underdiagnosed and underreported; it most commonly forms part of a quadrivalent valve disease. This review highlights the need for increased clinical and paraclinical vigilance when assessing the pulmonary valve in rheumatic heart disease.

title: Inflammation-Responsive baicalin-delivering glycocalyx-mimetic hydrogel-functionalized bioprosthetic valve for antithrombosis and immunomodulation.
authors: Lepeng Chen; Yanchang Feng; Xueyu Huang; Daisong Jiang; Cheng Zheng; Yunbing Wang
abstract: Valvular heart disease (VHD), a prevalent age-associated condition associated with high mortality, is primarily treated by prosthetic valve replacement. Bioprosthetic heart valves (BHVs) are increasingly preferred in clinical practice owing to their favorable hemodynamic performance and compatibility with transcatheter delivery. However, current glutaraldehyde crosslinking fails to confer antithrombotic, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory properties, leaving BHVs prone to thrombosis, oxidative stress, inflammation, and calcification, all of which accelerate structural valve deterioration (SVD) and shorten their lifespan. Herein, an inflammation-responsive, glycocalyx-mimetic hydrogel-functionalized BHV (BA@ALG-PP) was constructed using mussel-inspired catechol chemistry, which integrated a vascular glycocalyx-like layer with baicalin-loaded, reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive nanoparticles. With the introduction of a biocompatible glycocalyx-mimetic layer on the xenogeneic collagenous matrix, BA@ALG-PP exhibited improved antithrombotic and endothelialization performance, which was further confirmed in vivo by the rabbit intravascular implantation experiment. Moreover, the ROS-responsive nanoparticles effectively scavenged oxidative species and enabled stimulus-responsive on-demand release of anti-inflammatory molecule baicalin, thereby modulating local inflammatory responses. Transcriptional analysis of macrophages indicated that BA@ALG-PP regulated the expression of key inflammatory-related genes (Tnfaip3, Hmox1, Stat1, and Saa3) as well as suppressed pro-inflammatory signaling pathways, including NF-κB, MAPK, and JAK-STAT. Furthermore, BA@ALG-PP demonstrated improved anti-calcification property in the subcutaneous implantation experiments in rats. Collectively, this multifunctional strategy endows BHVs with synergistic antithrombotic, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and anti-calcification capabilities, thereby offering a potential strategy for improving BHV performance that warrants further investigation in large animal models and potentially mitigating factors contributing to SVD. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Glutaraldehyde-crosslinked bioprosthetic heart valves (BHVs) suffer from structural valve deterioration driven by thrombosis, oxidative stress, and chronic inflammation, yet current surface engineering strategies remain functionally limited. This study reports an inflammatory-responsive glycocalyx-mimetic hydrogel functionalized BHV (BA@ALG-PP) engineered via mussel-inspired catechol chemistry. The system integrates non-glutaraldehyde crosslinking, ROS-responsive baicalin release, and endothelial glycocalyx mimicry into a multifunctional platform. BA@ALG-PP demonstrates enhanced antithrombotic performance, accelerated endothelialization, effective ROS scavenging, and macrophage polarization from M1 to M2 phenotype through NF-κB, MAPK, and JAK-STAT pathway modulation. Furthermore, it significantly reduces calcification in vivo. This work establishes a comprehensive strategy for BHV crosslinking and surface engineering, offering a clinically translatable strategy to prolong BHV durability and improve patient outcomes.

title: Ten years of concomitant aortic and mitral replacement: trends, outcomes and the role of patient-prosthesis mismatch.
authors: Nicolò Azzola Guicciardi; Roberto Lorusso; Sofia Pavan; Benedetto Del Forno; Davide Margonato; Vincenzo Rizza; Andrea Mariani; Matteo Mazzola; Alessandro Castiglioni; Ottavio Alfieri; Eustachio Agricola; Francesco Maisano; Michele De Bonis
abstract:
Contemporary data comparing double mechanical prostheses (DMP) vs. double biological prostheses (DBP) for concomitant aortic and mitral valve replacement are scarce, and the cumulative hemodynamic burden of simultaneous prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) at both positions has never been systematically assessed.
DMP recipients had lower in-hospital mortality (1.9% vs. 15.2%; P = 0.010) and superior 7-year survival (91.3% vs. 67.7%; P = 0.003), but significantly higher stroke rates (32.2% vs. 5.0%; P = 0.023). Combined PPM occurred in 64.6% of DBP vs. 14.8% of DMP (P < 0.001).
Concomitant double valve replacement confirmed its high-risk profile, with an overall in-hospital mortality of 10.5%. DMP demonstrated superior unadjusted survival (7-year: 91.3% vs. 67.7%; P = 0.003) but significantly higher stroke risk (32.2% vs. 5.0%; P = 0.023), without differences in major bleeding rates at follow-up (8.2% vs. 11.3%; P = 0.478), although baseline differences precluded definitive prosthesis-type recommendations after multivariable adjustment. Combined PPM is highly prevalent after DBP (64.6%) and emerged as a univariable mortality predictor (hazard ratio 1.97; P = 0.046); given the exploratory nature of the cPPM definition and its collinearity with prosthesis type, this should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and warrants validation in larger, ideally multicenter, cohorts.

title: Echocardiographic Assessment and Clinical Applications of the Left Atrial Stiffness Index in Cardiovascular Disease.
authors: Xu Liu; Haomeng Xu; Yan Tong; Ying Ding; Shuai Wang
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract: The left atrial stiffness index is an emerging echocardiographic marker that integrates pressure-related burden and atrial reservoir deformation to provide a composite measure of left atrial pressure-deformation coupling. This review summarizes the pathophysiological basis of left atrial stiffness, the methodological principles underlying echocardiographic left atrial stiffness index assessment, and the current evidence supporting its clinical applications across cardiovascular diseases. The strongest evidence is available in heart failure and atrial fibrillation, in which increased left atrial stiffness index has been associated with adverse hemodynamics, exercise intolerance, rhythm recurrence, and adverse clinical outcomes. In hypertension, cardiomyopathies, valvular heart disease, and congenital or aortic disorders, available data suggest potential clinical relevance, although the evidence remains more heterogeneous and less mature; by contrast, evidence in ischemic, inflammatory, and stroke-related settings is still preliminary. Despite its physiological appeal, broader clinical adoption remains limited by methodological heterogeneity, variable thresholds, limited invasive validation, and uncertain incremental value beyond its component measures. At present, left atrial stiffness index is best positioned as an adjunctive marker for phenotyping, hemodynamic assessment, and risk stratification, particularly in heart failure and atrial fibrillation, pending further methodological harmonization and prospective disease-specific validation.

title: Percutaneous Removal of a Tricuspid Valve Vegetation Using the AngioVac System in a Young Woman Who Injects Drugs.
authors: Tomasz Skowerski; Andrzej Kułach; Marek Grabka; Piotr Pysz; Paulina Kudzia; Eliza Adamczyk-Filipek; Radosław Gocoł; Grzegorz Smolka
abstract: Right-sided infective endocarditis (RSIE) is a difficult clinical problem, particularly among people who inject drugs (PWID), in whom large tricuspid vegetations may be complicated by severe regurgitation and septic pulmonary embolization. We describe a woman in her twenties with tricuspid valve infective endocarditis and bilateral cavitary pulmonary lesions consistent with septic emboli, in whom the vegetation enlarged from 18 × 11 mm to 18 × 20 mm and tricuspid regurgitation (TR) progressed from moderate to severe (vena contracta 12 mm, effective regurgitant orifice area 1.5 cm2, regurgitant volume 110 mL) over ten days of empirical anti-staphylococcal therapy. Surgery was considered by an individualized Heart Team assessment of the complete clinical course, but the patient declined open-heart surgery. After multidisciplinary Heart Team discussion, transesophageal echocardiography (TEE)-guided percutaneous aspiration with the AngioVac system was undertaken as an individualized debulking and source-control strategy, not as an equivalent alternative to surgery. Under general anesthesia, bilateral femoral venous access was obtained and seven aspiration passes retrieved four large vegetation fragments, with no residual intracardiac mass on completion TEE. Culture of the aspirated material yielded Serratia marcescens and Escherichia coli, neither of which was covered by the empirical regimen, which was replaced by susceptibility-guided ciprofloxacin and co-trimoxazole; ceftazidime was added when Pseudomonas aeruginosa was later isolated from blood. Residual regurgitation arose from a flail, prolapsing posterior leaflet rather than from mass effect-a finding that may reflect pre-existing infective leaflet destruction, leaflet injury during aspiration, or both-and was quantitatively reduced three to four weeks after the procedure (vena contracta 6 mm, effective regurgitant orifice area 0.55 cm2, regurgitant volume 36 mL); at six months it was moderate-to-severe and stable, with preserved right ventricular function (TAPSE 30 mm) and no recurrent vegetation. This case supports a potential diagnostic and therapeutic role for AngioVac-assisted debulking as an individualized adjunct in highly selected patients with RSIE who refuse surgery, with the caveat that aspiration reduces vegetation and embolic burden without correcting the underlying valvular lesion.

title: Advanced Carcinoid Tricuspid Valve Disease Associated with Delayed Recognition and Loss of the Interventional Window in a Patient with Ileal Neuroendocrine Tumor: A Case Report.
authors: Ionela Cotfas; Cosmin Banceu; Horațiu Suciu; Klara Brînzaniuc; Ileana Voichița Sirbu
abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Carcinoid heart disease remains one of the most serious complications of carcinoid syndrome, yet cardiac involvement may still be recognized late, when valvular damage is already advanced and treatment options are limited. Case Presentation: We report a 70-year-old man with a well-differentiated ileal neuroendocrine tumor (NET G2, Ki-67 up to 5%), diagnosed in December 2019. Over six years, the disease progressed with liver metastases, markedly rising 24 h urinary 5-HIAA levels and clinically active carcinoid syndrome, and was treated sequentially with somatostatin analogues, everolimus and 177Lu-DOTATOC. Throughout this period, oncological evaluation was frequent, whereas structured cardiac assessment was essentially absent until 2025. When the patient was referred for evaluation for transcatheter tricuspid repair, echocardiography demonstrated advanced carcinoid tricuspid valve disease with severe regurgitation, mild stenosis, marked leaflet thickening and tethering, and a coaptation gap of 17 mm-far beyond the ~7 mm threshold associated with favorable edge-to-edge repair and the >10 mm range associated with poor outcome. Because of the advanced valve remodeling and the overall clinical burden, the patient was not a candidate for transcatheter edge-to-edge repair or surgery and subsequently died. Conclusions: This case illustrates how carcinoid heart disease can progress beyond correctability and supports regular echocardiographic surveillance in patients with carcinoid syndrome, so that valve involvement is identified while intervention is still anatomically feasible.

title: Digital image analysis-based quantification of p53 immunohistochemistry in gastric cancer: a systematic comparison of three-tier cutoff-derivation strategies in tissue microarrays.
authors: Jaeyoung Ahn; Kyungeun Kim; Hee-Jung Yang; Boram Song; Dong Hoon Kim; Yumin Chung; Seoung Wan Chae
journal: Journal of pathology and translational medicine
abstract:
p53 immunohistochemistry (IHC) is a common surrogate for TP53 alteration, but in gastric cancer, its concordance is imperfect and depends on a non-standardized cutoff. Digital pathology enables H-score quantification, yet neither its reproducibility nor the choice of cutoff- derivation strategy has been systematically compared.
A semi-automated digital workflow quantified p53 IHC in tissue microarrays from 528 gastric cancer patients. Tumor cells were detected with a deep-learning model (InstanSeg), and nuclear staining was expressed as a continuous H-score (0-300). Reproducibility was assessed at each observer-dependent step. Five thresholding strategies were compared: manual cutoffs, tertiles, log-rank optimization, the extended Youden index, and volume under the receiver operating characteristic surface (VUS). The latter two strategies used the manual three-tier IHC interpretation as the reference standard.
Quantification was reproducible: two independent manual interpretations agreed in 91.7% of cores (κ = 0.845). The H-score was robust to the detection algorithm (intraclass correlation coefficient, 0.990) and to repeated threshold determination (0.954). H-scores were right-skewed (median, 45.5), and the strategies yielded distinct cutoffs (8.0-27.6 and 78.6-106.0). Log-rank optimization provided the widest separation but lost significance after multiplicity adjustment (p = .168). The extended Youden and VUS cutoffs were statistically indistinguishable. As a supporting check, all classifications showed nominal overall-survival separation, with low and overexpression faring similarly worse than wild-type.
Digital p53 IHC quantification was reproducible at each observer-dependent step. The extended Youden and VUS criteria performed equivalently; therefore, we propose Youden as a reasonable default, pending validation and TP53 correlation.

title: Retrospective multi-reader evaluation of a Deep-Learning-based cancer detection model in Contrast-Enhanced Mammography.
authors: Amr Farouk Ibrahim Moustafa; Clement Jailin; Laurence Vancamberg; Sara Mohamed; Pablo Milioni De Carvalho; Razvan Iordache; Eman Faker Kamal; Mohammed Mohammed Mohammed Gomaa; Rasha Mohammed Kamal
abstract:
To evaluate the clinical impact of a deep-learning-based computer-aided diagnostic tool applied to contrast-enhanced mammography on radiologists' diagnostic accuracy and reading efficiency.
In this retrospective single-centre study, 150 contrast-enhanced mammography examinations were interpreted by five radiologists. Each case was read and annotated twice in two sequential sessions: first without assistance and then with the computer-aided diagnostic tool, with a minimum 4-week washout period. Diagnostic performance was assessed at lesion and breast levels using free-response receiver operating characteristic analysis, area under the curve, and false-positive rate. Reading time for one radiologist was recorded as an exploratory measure.
The computer-aided diagnostic tool was associated with improved lesion-level performance for most radiologists, with a mean increase in the area under the free-response curve of 0.030 ± 0.018. At 89% sensitivity, false-positive findings decreased by an average of 11.4% ± 24% across all radiologists. No improvement was observed at the breast level, possibly related to the tool's single-view analysis and dataset characteristics. An exploratory analysis showed a 31% reduction in reading time for one radiologist.
Integration of a deep learning-based computer-aided diagnostic tool into contrast-enhanced mammography was associated with improved lesion-level diagnostic performance and reduced false-positive findings, without measurable improvement at the breast level.
To our knowledge, this study provides one of the early clinical evaluations of a deep learning-based computer-aided diagnostic tool for contrast-enhanced mammography, suggesting potential improvements in lesion-level diagnostic performance and workflow efficiency while highlighting current limitations at the breast level.

title: Artificial intelligence in personalized internal dosimetry for radiopharmaceutical therapy: a narrative mini-review.
authors: Mohammed A Jowhari
abstract: Personalized internal radiation dosimetry supports individualized radiopharmaceutical therapy but remains difficult to implement because workflows require repeated quantitative imaging, segmentation, registration, kinetic modeling, and absorbed-dose calculation. This mini-review summarizes current evidence on artificial intelligence across the personalized dosimetry workflow and considers clinical readiness. A narrative PubMed search was completed in early 2026 and covered peer-reviewed studies published from 2015 to early 2026. Studies addressing artificial intelligence, machine learning, or deep learning in quantitative image reconstruction, segmentation, registration, time-activity curve estimation, absorbed-dose calculation, or clinical decision support were considered. Studies reporting quantitative performance or validation results were prioritized. Deep learning reduced yttrium-90 single-photon emission computed tomography reconstruction error from 149.5% ± 31.2% to 9.2% ± 1.7%; lesion dose-rate error was 8.6% ± 5.7% in virtual-patient testing. Learning-based registration reduced computation time from about 50 s to under 6 s. Single-time-point approaches can simplify imaging, and recent machine learning work has explored prediction of organ effective half-life. Automated segmentation methods show improving reproducibility, whereas evidence for artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support remains mainly retrospective and single-center. Artificial intelligence applications in reconstruction and segmentation appear closer to clinical readiness, while decision-support applications still require prospective, multicenter validation.

title: AI-powered spectral CT analysis for clinical decision support in carotid vulnerable plaque detection: a deep learning approach.
authors: Yunzhe Ni; Tianyu Zhang; Zonghui Huang; Yuguang Wang; Guochao Han; Yuan Lin; Bo Liu; Wennan Lin; Hui Li
journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
abstract:
Carotid vulnerable plaques (CVPs) represent a major cause of ischemic stroke, yet current diagnostic methods lack sufficient precision for early detection. Spectral computed tomography (CT) enables detailed plaque characterization, but its clinical utility depends on advanced analytical techniques.
A Fourier Transform-enhanced U-Net model was developed using spectral CT data from 214 patients at Qiqihar Medical College. Transfer learning was applied for carotid segmentation, supported by extensive data augmentation and ten-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). A patient-level independent test set was reserved to evaluate model performance.
The FTC-enhanced U-Net achieved a Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.89 and an intersection over union (IoU) of 0.80, accurately delineating arterial and plaque boundaries. Stable classification performance was maintained across plaque risk levels, with accuracies of 86% for low-risk, 83% for medium-risk, and 87% for high-risk plaques. Ten-fold cross-validation yielded an AUC of 0.88 ± 0.03, an accuracy of 85.3% ± 2.1%, and an F1-score of 0.84 ± 0.02, confirming strong robustness and generalizability.
Artificial intelligence (AI)-based predictive models derived from spectral CT imaging show substantial potential for early diagnosis and prognostic assessment of CVPs. The FTC-enhanced U-Net provides an efficient and reliable tool for clinical decision support, facilitating broader adoption of AI in vascular imaging and improving diagnostic precision and patient management.

title: MFCAMNet: predicting miRNA-disease associations by multi-feature cascade attention mechanism network.
authors: Yuanxing Wang; Chen Yang; Yucheng Zhang
abstract: Drive by the rapid envolution of deep-learning techniques, a large body of biological experiments bas has uncovered extensive associations between microRNAs (miRNAs) and complex human diseases, hig- hlighting the pivotal roles of miRNAs in pathogenesis. Elucidating these associations is essential for understanding disease mechanisms and developing preventive strategies. Traditional wet-lab validati- on, however, is notoriously labor- and resource-intensive, creating an urgent demand for efficient computational tools that can prioritize the most promising miRNA-disease candidates. Existing predictors predominantly rely on a single category of handcrafted features, thereby overlooking the complementary information embedded in multiple, heterogeneous data sources. Although a few recent attempts integrate diverse features, they usually exploit only a limited subset and fail to capture the intricate, non-linear relationships among them. To address these limitations, we propose MFCAMNet, a Multi-Feature fusion and Cross-Self-Attention model for MiRNA-Disease association prediction. Firstly, we construct multiple similarity matrices and employ two independent autoencoders with multi-source feature attention to obtain deep features of miRNA and disease to extract the inherent relationships between multiple features. Secondly, the proposed model employs element-level addition, element-level multiplication, and concatenation operations to generate miRNA-disease pair features with rich information. Finally, we use the encoder structure of the transformer to fuse the three deep features and predict all potential miRNA disease associations. We conducted comprehensive evaluations on the public HMDD v2.0 and HMDD v3.2 benchmark datasets. MFCAMNet achieved average AUCs of 0.9455 and 0.9420 under 5-fold and 10-fold cross-validation on HMDD v2.0, respectively, and an AUC of 0.9578 under 5-fold cross-validation on HMDD v3.2, outperforming state-of-the-art competitors. Case studies on breast, esophageal, and lung cancers further corroborate the reliability and practical utility of the proposed method.

title: A deep learning framework for threshold-free relative gene expression ranking from histone modification signals.
authors: Abdul Munif; Amitava Datta; Zhaoyu Li; Max Ward
abstract:
Current methods for predicting gene expression from histone modifications rely on arbitrary binary classification thresholds such as the median to distinguish between high and low expression for genes. This approach lacks biological justification, creates dataset-dependent classifications, and ignores the relative regulatory relationships between genes that are often more biologically meaningful than absolute cutoffs.
We developed a deep learning method using pairwise ranking to determine the relative gene expression levels between gene pairs based on their histone modification signals. The approach adopted the DirectRanker architecture, which enforces antisymmetry by construction through a twin-subnet design with asymmetric subtraction, and was evaluated against three baseline classifiers (Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and SVM Linear) on identical features and data splits. Ablation testing across all 31 non-empty subsets of five histone marks (H3K4me3, H3K9ac, H3K9me3, H3K27ac, H3K27me3) was conducted to identify their individual contributions. Datasets were strictly partitioned (80% training, 10% validation, 10% testing) with gene-level separation to prevent data leakage, and all experiments were repeated across five independent random seeds. Four datasets were analysed: two normal adult liver cell datasets (Donor 3 and Donor 4 from NCBI GEO GSE19465) and two HepG2 hepatocellular carcinoma cell line datasets (ENCSR134DWG and GSE76344).
Multi-mark combinations anchored by active histone marks (H3K27ac, H3K4me3, H3K9ac) consistently drove predictive performance, with the best combinations achieving AUROC values of 0.833-0.867 and test accuracies of 74-78% across datasets. DirectRanker attained AUPRC values of 0.819-0.856, closely matching or exceeding Random Forest on precision-recall performance. Repressive marks (H3K9me3, H3K27me3) consistently underperformed when used in isolation, with single-mark models achieving test accuracies of only 50-66%. DirectRanker produced substantially higher antisymmetry scores (0.961-0.983) than all baseline classifiers (0.787-0.851), confirming logically consistent pairwise predictions. Performance plateaued at four- to five-mark combinations, reflecting correlated predictive signal among the active marks within the promoter-proximal feature space.
The pairwise ranking framework provides a principled alternative to threshold-based classification, enabling relative gene expression comparisons without arbitrary binarisation cutoffs. While Random Forest achieved marginally higher accuracy, DirectRanker's structural antisymmetry guarantee makes it the more suitable choice for applications requiring a globally coherent gene ranking. Active promoter marks carry the majority of the predictive signal, while the performance saturation with increasing mark combinations reflects overlapping information content rather than biological redundancy.

title: GenVarLoader: an accelerated dataloader for applying deep learning to personalized genomics.
authors: David Laub; Aaron Ho; Loukik Raina; Jeff Jaureguy; Adam Klie; Rany M Salem; Graham McVicker; Hannah Carter
abstract:
Deep learning models can predict the functional impact of genetic variants. However, training and applying these sequence models to personalized genome sequences are severely constrained by the computational burden of storing and reading massive datasets.
We developed GenVarLoader, an accelerated dataloader that creates personalized genomic sequences and functional tracks on-the-fly to overcome these bottlenecks. GenVarLoader stores this personalized genomic data in formats specifically optimized for machine learning. Our tool reads variants up to 26,000 times faster than a pre-subset BCF, loads personalized data up to 130 times faster than tuned FASTA and pyBigWig pipelines, and reduces storage approximately 2,000-fold compared to existing alternatives.
By eliminating severe data loading bottlenecks, GenVarLoader ensures efficient model training and inference. It provides a scalable solution for integrating biobank-scale personalized genomic data with deep learning applications.

title: Multicentric development and validation of a fully automated artificial intelligence system for planning medial open wedge high tibial osteotomy on weight-bearing anterior-posterior long leg radiographs: The ISAKOS John Joyce Award 2025.
authors: Marco-Christopher Rupp; Claudio E von Schacky; Felix J Lindner; Matthias J Feucht; Yannick Ehmann; Lorenz Fritsch; Alexandros Doucas; Sami Haddadin; Florian Hinterwimmer; Matthias Jung; Maximilian F Russe; Rüdiger von Eisenhart-Rothe; Sebastian Siebenlist; Nikolas J Wilhelm
journal: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA
abstract:
Preoperative planning, currently performed by orthopaedic surgeons (OS), is essential for successful osteotomy, but is labour-intensive and error-prone. As such, there is significant potential in the use of automated artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms to augment the abilities of OS in managing lower extremity pathologies in a high-volume task that demands high precision and reliability. The aim was to develop a deep learning (DL) system capable of fully autonomous planning a medial open wedge high tibial osteotomy (mow-HTO) on weight bearing anterior posterior (AP) long leg radiographs (LLR) and to validate its agreement with an expert-derived reference standard, its reliability and processing time of the DL model compared to expert OS on multicentric test data sets (two institutions).
A total of 594 patients (age 41.1 ± 13.2 years, 182 female) who underwent osteotomy between 01/2014 and 01/2021 were retrospectively enrolled. Manual annotations for lower extremity alignment and high tibial landmarks were performed on AP LLR radiographs. The data set was divided into training (60%, n = 399), validation (10%, n = 59) and hold-out testing (30%, n = 136), with an additional external dataset (n = 100) for further testing. A DL system with twelve expert networks was trained to identify relevant landmarks for HTO planning. The DL model was then tested on fully automated planning of a medial open wedge HTO based on (1) the desired postoperative intersection of the mechanical axis with the tibial plateau (%-based) and (2) the desired femorotibial axis (°-based). Agreement with the expert-derived reference, reliability and processing time were compared with three expert OS using FDA-approved preoperative planning software on the test data sets.
For preoperative alignment parameter analysis, compared to the ground truth, human preoperative accuracy ranged from 0.13° ± 0.10° to 1.06° ± 1.4°, interrater reliability ranged from intraclass correlation (ICC) 0.84-1.0 and clinically acceptable accuracy ranged from 72% to 100%. Preoperative accuracy of the DL model ranged from 0.22° ± 0.18° to 1.04° ± 1.28°, interrater reliability ranged from ICC 0.93-1.0 and clinically acceptable accuracy ranged from 91% to 100%. For the planning of the osteotomy gap, compared to the ground truth, human accuracy ranged from 0.46 ± 0.65 mm to 0.5 ± 0.88 mm (%-based) and 0.43 ± 0.55 to 0.52 ± 0.75 mm (°-based), reliability ranged from ICC 0.9-0.96 and 0.95-0.97 and clinically acceptable accuracy was 93.6%-96.0% (%-based) and 89.8%-93.9% (°-based). For the DL model, the accuracy was 0.53 ± 0.63 mm (%-based) and 0.44 ± 0.53 mm (°-based), reliability was ICC 0.99 (both methods) and clinically acceptable accuracy was 98.1% (%-based) and 96.2% (°-based). The DL-model significantly and substantially outperformed the OS in intrarater reliability (0.88 vs. 1.0) and processing time for a fully automated alignment analysis (25.3 ± 0.8 s vs. 148.7 ± 10.1 s, p < 0.001).
The developed DL model enabled fully automated mow-HTO planning on AP long-leg radiographs with reliability comparable to that of expert OS while significantly reducing processing time and improving measurement consistency. These suggest that DL-based systems may assist orthopaedic providers by accelerating and standardising osteotomy planning.
Level III, retrospective comparative study.

title: Automated MRI Series Classification Across Heterogeneous Datasets Using Limited Manual Annotation.
authors: Ryan Fishman; Evan Calabrese
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
abstract: The purpose of this study is to determine the smallest tested fraction of manually labeled training data required for a multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) classifier to achieve satisfactory MRI series classification performance (macro-F1 ≥ 0.80) across five heterogeneous public MRI datasets using digital imaging and communications in medicine (DICOM) metadata, image data, or both. This retrospective study included 3804 examinations and 14,054 MRI series from five public DICOM datasets spanning brain, knee, lumbar spine, liver, and breast MRI, accessed February-April 2026. AI classification models included a random forest classifier using DICOM header metadata, a deep convolutional neural network classifier using the geometric center slice of each MRI series, and decision-fusion models. Models were trained with 5%-40% of studies manually labeled in 5-percentage-point increments, with additional 1%-4% fractions for the knee and lumbar spine. Model performance was evaluated on the remaining studies using study-level splits across five random seeds. Results were summarized as mean ± standard deviation. Zero-label unsupervised clustering results were evaluated separately on the full dataset. The macro-F1 target was reached at the smallest tested training fraction of 1% in the lumbar spine (0.945 ± 0.013), at 2% in the knee (0.818 ± 0.006), at 10% in the brain (0.872 ± 0.027), and at 20% in the liver (0.827 ± 0.016) and the breast (0.847 ± 0.012). The best-performing model differed by dataset, reflecting different contributions from metadata versus image data. Across five separately evaluated public MRI datasets, at least one header-based, image-based, or combined model achieved macro-F1 ≥ 0.80 using no more than 20% manually labeled studies.

title: Automated Multi-class Segmentation of Mandibular Odontogenic Cysts and the Mandibular Canal on CBCT Images Using a Hybrid Deep Learning Framework.
authors: Adalet Çelebi; Dilan Aykanat; Özgür Tonkal; Deniz Bora Küçük; Ayşe Özcan Küçük; Muammer Türkoğlu; Fethi Atıl
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
abstract: Mandibular odontogenic cysts can complicate surgical planning if located near the mandibular canal. Accurate delineation of both structures is therefore clinically important. This study presents a deep learning-based method for simultaneously segmenting mandibular odontogenic cysts and the mandibular canal in cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images. The developed method relies on a hybrid deep learning architecture integrating a ConvNeXt-Base encoder, a Dilated Context Block, a U-Net-based decoder, and a Deep Supervision mechanism. This framework simultaneously segments the mandibular canal and odontogenic cyst regions within the same architecture, promoting multi-scale contextual feature learning. We evaluated the performance of the proposed method using fivefold cross-validation experiments on a real-world clinical CBCT dataset comprising 103 patient images. We assessed segmentation performance using overlap-based metrics together with boundary-aware HD95 and ASSD metrics. The experimental results demonstrated that the model achieved a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 76.28% ± 1.83%. Excluding the background class yielded macro IoU and macro F1-score values of 64.46% ± 2.74% and 77.00% ± 1.89%, respectively. Meanwhile, the weighted IoU and weighted F1-score values were 78.71% ± 4.25% and 87.63% ± 2.63%, respectively. In boundary-based evaluations, the mandibular canal had an HD95 of 2.44 ± 2.98 mm and an ASSD of 0.45 ± 0.30 mm. The corresponding values for odontogenic cysts were 5.59 ± 3.65 mm and 1.43 ± 0.88 mm, respectively. These results suggest that the mandibular canal is more consistently delineated, while cyst segmentation remains more challenging, particularly at irregular and low-contrast boundaries. The proposed framework allows for the simultaneous and objective segmentation of mandibular odontogenic cysts and the mandibular canal within a unified, multi-class CBCT analysis framework. By providing reproducible delineation of both structures, this method could serve as a technical foundation for future quantitative analyses of lesion-canal relationships. However, further validation using larger, multicenter, volumetric CBCT datasets is required before clinical translation.

title: Hair Segmentation and Skin Characterization on Macroscopic Dermatological Images for Laser Treatment Parameterization.
authors: Alex Navarro Navarro; Marc Arriaga Hidalgo; Carlos Moreno Rubio; Maxime Talarmain; Noelia Vaquero Gallardo
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
abstract: Current light-based devices, such as laser hair removal, intense pulsed light (IPL), vascular laser therapy, and dermatologic phototherapy, are widely used in clinical dermatology but rely heavily on subjective manual parameterization or uncalibrated point-based colorimeters. To overcome these limitations, this work presents a unified system for hair segmentation and skin characterization in macroscopic dermatological images. Unlike most existing literature that relies on dermoscopic datasets captured under highly controlled conditions, our approach is specifically designed for macroscopic images that replicate real clinical laser treatments. The proposed pipeline integrates a custom-trained variant of the YOLOv9 deep learning architecture for instance segmentation and classical image processing within a single workflow to extract objective skin and hair parameters such as phototype, hair density, color, and thickness. A color calibration stage using spectrophotometric measurements ensures accurate feature estimation regardless of illumination conditions. Experimental results show competitive segmentation metrics (mAP@50 ≈ 0.80) on a custom dataset featuring short, shaved hairs, typical of pre-treatment scenarios. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed pipeline in providing the objective, foundational skin and hair features required for future automated laser parameterization, paving the way for its extension to broader light-based medical therapies.

title: Wavelet Scalogram-Based Nystagmus Classification for Automated Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo Subtype Diagnosis.
authors: Yerin Lee; Sena Lee; Hyun Su Lee; Tae Hoon Kong; Young Joon Seo; Sejung Yang
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
abstract: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) is the most common cause of vestibular vertigo, yet accurate diagnosis remains challenging without specialist expertise. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an artificial intelligence (AI)-based diagnostic algorithm for BPPV using video-nystagmography (VNG) recordings. A total of 1352 VNG recordings were collected from patients with posterior semicircular canal (PSCC) BPPV (n = 234), lateral semicircular canal (LSCC) BPPV (canalolithiasis, n = 188; cupulolithiasis, n = 58), and healthy controls (n = 224) at a single tertiary referral hospital, yielding 1738 signal segments (1312 nystagmus segments annotated by two otolaryngologists and 426 normal segments). Eye trajectory signals were extracted using a deep learning-based VNG eye-tracking algorithm, transformed into two-dimensional (2D) scalogram representations via continuous wavelet transform (CWT), and classified using task-specific backbone architectures selected through systematic comparison under a patient-level data split. Ablation analysis showed that CWT-based 2D representations significantly outperformed raw one-dimensional (1D) time-series baselines. The final models achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) values of 0.974 for horizontal and 0.961 for torsional nystagmus classification. For BPPV subtype diagnosis, recording-level accuracy was 0.935 for the PSCC and 0.938 for the LSCC evaluation; F1-scores exceeded 0.84 for all PSCC classes and ranged from 0.59 to 0.98 for LSCC classes, with canalolithiasis variants outperforming cupulolithiasis variants. These findings suggest the feasibility of AI-assisted BPPV diagnosis from VNG recordings.

title: Human-in-the-loop LLM-assisted thematic analysis: A validated, reproducible tutorial for large-scale qualitative research.
authors: Mandana Jafarian
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support qualitative research, yet clear methodological frameworks for integrating them into thematic analysis remain limited. A central challenge is how to scale qualitative coding with LLM assistance while preserving methodological rigor and reproducibility. This tutorial presents a structured, human-in-the-loop workflow for conducting large-scale thematic analysis with LLM support. Grounded in inductive and hybrid approaches to thematic analysis (Braun & Clarke, 2006), the workflow proceeds in three phases. First, researchers conduct manual thematic analysis on a subset of data to establish an initial codebook and assess relevance. Second, the same subset is analyzed using an LLM to iteratively refine prompts and evaluate alignment between human and model outputs. Third, the validated approach is applied to the full corpus using a modular four-step pipeline: key-idea extraction, chunk-level thematic coding, theme consolidation, and clustering, with iterative human verification through random sampling of outputs. We demonstrate the workflow using 2,952 publicly available Reddit posts. Structured prompt design and JSON-formatted outputs enable traceability between themes and source data and support reproducible analysis. Prompt engineering is treated as an iterative analytic process rather than a one-time instruction. Under controlled conditions, human and LLM coding showed high agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.91). All prompts, code, and reproducibility materials are openly available via an Open Science Framework repository. By providing detailed implementation guidance, embedded validation procedures, and safeguards against common failure modes such as hallucination and overgeneralization, this tutorial offers a practical and extensible framework for integrating LLMs into qualitative research across domains.

title: Factors influencing surface ozone concentrations in Wuhan: an interpretable machine learning analysis.
authors: Dong-Yang Yang; Su-Ying Chai; Ji-Xiong Wang; Jiu-Yuan Yu; Zeng-Zeng Yu; Yan Cao; Yi-Yao Wen; Fang Bai; Wei-Hua Zhao; Wei-Jie Guo
abstract: Ground-level ozone (O3) has become a major challenge for air quality improvement in China, but its short-term variability is controlled by complex interactions among pollutant persistence, precursor conditions, and meteorological factors. In this study, hourly air quality observations and ERA5 reanalysis meteorological data for an urban monitoring site in Wuhan during 2019-2025 were integrated to evaluate O3 temporal variability and interpretable machine learning prediction. Three models, namely, deep neural network (DNN), random forest (RF), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), were compared using baseline and lag-enhanced feature sets, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to interpret predictive contributions. O3 remained at relatively high levels during 2019-2025, with exceedances of the national grade II standard in 2019, 2023, and 2024, while most primary pollutants generally declined. O3 exhibited a unimodal diurnal cycle with afternoon peaks at 14:00-16:00 and a seasonal pattern of summer > spring > autumn > winter. The enhanced XGBoost model achieved the best short-term prediction performance, with R2 = 0.9756 and RMSE = 6.35 μg m-3 on the test set. SHAP analysis showed that the 1-h lagged O3 concentration was the dominant predictor, indicating strong short-term persistence rather than independent chemical forcing. NO2 and lagged NO2 showed negative predictive contributions, consistent with the expected role of NO titration under high-NOₓ conditions, whereas temperature and radiation-related variables showed positive contributions. These results suggest that interpretable machine learning can help identify the statistical conditions associated with O3 variability, but the absence of direct VOC observations means that O3 sensitivity and VOC-related control implications should be further verified using VOC measurements or chemical transport/observation-based modeling.

title: ReScale4DL: balancing pixel and contextual information for enhanced bioimage segmentation.
authors: Mariana G Ferreira; Bruno M Saraiva; António D Brito; Mariana G Pinho; Ricardo Henriques; Estibaliz Gómez-de-Mariscal
abstract: Deep learning is the state-of-the-art approach for bioimage segmentation. However, it presents a paradox regarding image resolution: counterintuitively, deep learning segmentation performance can improve with lower image resolutions. This phenomenon is particularly significant in microscopy, where high-resolution acquisitions come with substantial costs in throughput, storage requirements and potential photodamage. We systematically evaluate how image resolution impacts segmentation by training popular architectures on datasets downsampled to 6-50% of their original resolution, mimicking lower-magnification acquisitions. Compared with models trained on native-resolution images, segmentation accuracy either improves (by up to 25% of mean Intersection over Union (IoU)) or degrades minimally (< 5% of mean IoU) when using images downsampled by up to fourfold (25% of the original resolution). Downsampling proportionally increases information throughput while reducing storage requirements and inference time. These findings provide practical guidelines for creating efficient, sustainable and cost-effective bioimaging pipelines that reduce data and computing needs while optimising microscopy techniques.

title: Net carbon losses in Central African forests revealed by high-resolution biomass change maps.
authors: Liang Wan; Philippe Ciais; Aurélien de Truchis; Yidi Xu; Martin Brandt; Jérôme Chave; Clément Bourgoin; Jean-Pierre Wigneron; Jean-François Bastin; Wei Li; Youngryel Ryu; Shidong Liu; David Purnell; Ibrahim Fayad; Le Bienfaiteur Sagang; Arthur Vander Linden; Timothée Besisa; Pierre Ploton
abstract: Dense humid forests in Central Africa hold vast biomass carbon stocks but are increasingly affected by small-scale disturbances that are difficult to detect with current satellite observations. Here, we generate 10 m canopy height maps for 2019-2022 using deep learning with spaceborne lidar and Sentinel-1/-2 imagery, and derive aboveground biomass changes at 30 m resolution. The maps reveal widespread small disturbance patches, 87% smaller than 1 ha. These account for 48% of biomass carbon gains in regrowing forests and 37% of carbon losses from deforestation. We estimate a net forest carbon loss of -58 ± 14 Tg C yr-1, with gross losses of -126  ±  21 Tg C yr-1 partially offset by gains of 68  ±  10 Tg C yr-1. The Democratic Republic of the Congo emerges as a net carbon source (-46  ±  11 Tg C yr-1), representing 79% of the regional loss, primarily due to degradation, despite having the largest carbon gains in young secondary forests. Our remote-sensing estimates of national carbon budgets are broadly consistent with country-level inventories and bookkeeping model estimates, paving the way for spatially explicit and transparent carbon monitoring.

title: Predicting trail-making test performance using 7-Tesla structural cerebral MRI.
authors: Gereon J Schnellbächer; Ravichandran Rajkumar; Tanja Veselinović; Shukti Ramkiran; Jana Hagen; Maria Collee; N Jon Shah; Irene Neuner; Jürgen Dammers
abstract: Psychopharmaceutical therapy has seen a lack of improvement in efficacy, highlighting the need for a more individualized treatment approach that optimally leverages pharmaceutical effects. To achieve this, it is necessary to identify factors that can predict psychological attributes and treatment outcomes. We hypothesize that brain morphology may serve as a predictor of performance in psychological tests. A 7-Tesla-MRI system was used to measure 74 transdiagnostic patients and 41 healthy controls. Values for grey matter volume (GMV), cortical thickness and gyrification based on the Schaefer 100 Atlas for parcellation were determined. Using this morphological data, performance in a Trail-Making Test (TMT) - A and B was predicted with the help of a deep learning model. A SHAP analysis was conducted to identify the key variables important for the model. The accuracy in predicting TMT performance was very good at 0.795. The most decisive feature influencing predictions was gyrification. Areas indicating inter-group differences were focused in the frontal cortex, as well as in temporal and parietal regions. Morphological characteristics can predict test performance with high accuracy. These results support the implementation of a transdiagnostic approach in clinical practice to better address the underlying pathophysiology. Symptom prediction based on neuroimaging data appears to be an achievable goal.

title: Performance of artificial intelligence-based coronary CT angiography-derived fractional flow reserve across cohorts with different prevalence of obstructive coronary artery disease.
authors: Casper F Coerkamp; Merel Gommers; Richard A P Takx; Roel S Driessen; Victor A Verpalen; Paul Knaapen; Ivana Išgum; Nick S Nurmohamed; José P S Henriques; Nils R Planken
abstract:
Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides accurate anatomical assessment of coronary stenosis severity but has limited ability to determine lesion-specific ischemia as assessed by invasive fractional flow reserve (FFR). We aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of an artificial intelligence-based deep learning CCTA-derived FFR model (CT-FFRAI) in cohorts undergoing CCTA and invasive FFR as part of a study protocol and a real-world cohort undergoing invasive FFR based on suspected coronary artery disease on CCTA in routine clinical care.
Diagnostic performance of CT-FFRAI (CorEx, SPIMED-AI) was evaluated using an intention-to-diagnose approach and compared with CCTA using 50% and 70% stenosis thresholds, with invasive FFR as reference standard. In the PACIFIC-1 study cohort, 208 patients underwent CCTA and invasive FFR assessment of all major coronary vessels irrespective of CCTA findings. The real-world cohort included 202 patients with at least one CCTA-defined lesion ≥70% stenosis who underwent ICA with invasive FFR.
In the PACIFIC-1 cohort (612 vessels), per-vessel diagnostic accuracy was comparable between CT-FFRAI (77%), when using a CCTA based ≥50% stenosis threshold (76%; P = 0.689), and when using a ≥70% stenosis threshold (74%; P = 0.183). In the real-world cohort (325 vessels), CT-FFRAI demonstrated higher per-vessel diagnostic accuracy (63%) compared with CCTA using ≥50% and ≥70% stenosis thresholds (52% and 57%, respectively; P < 0.001 and P = 0.034). Net reclassification improvement for CT-FFRAI beyond CCTA alone using ≥50% and ≥70% stenosis thresholds was 7.9% (P = 0.256) and 17.7% (P = 0.012) in the PACIFIC-1 cohort, compared with 23.2% (P < 0.001) and 13.6% (P = 0.070) in the real-world cohort, respectively.
CT-FFRAI may outperform anatomic assessment alone, with diagnostic accuracy depending on the prevalence of obstructive coronary artery disease and the range of stenosis severities among vessels undergoing invasive FFR assessment.

title: Design of Screening Cardiometabolic Opportunities Using Transformative Echocardiography Artificial Intelligence (SCOUT-Echo-AI).
authors: Sahir Eusuff; Jay Kim; Zara Fatima; Dilek Yalcinkaya; Yuki Sahashi; Alexander Sandhu; Long H Nguyen; Andrew P Ambrosy; Paul P Cheng; Stephanie T Chang; Alan S Go; Faraz S Ahmad; Amanda Cheung; Susan Cheng; Alan C Kwan; David Ouyang
abstract:
Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is highly prevalent among individuals with cardiovascular disease, but often remains undiagnosed until advanced sequelae such as fibrotic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma develop. ​​Transthoracic echocardiography routinely captures incidental subcostal views of the liver that are not used clinically. The EchoNet-Liver algorithm uses artificial intelligence (AI) to predict the presence of liver disease based on routine clinical echocardiograms. Prospective evaluation in real-world practice is needed to understand the clinical utility and impact of AI-enabled opportunistic liver disease screening.
The SCOUT-Echo-AI study is a single-arm, prospective, multicenter, open-label pragmatic interventional trial that will be conducted across six diverse U.S. healthcare systems (Kaiser Permanente Northern California, Stanford Healthcare, Cedars-Sinai Medical Center, University of California Los Angeles, Northwestern Medicine, and Massachusetts General Brigham). Routine echocardiograms will be analyzed by the EchoNet-Liver AI algorithm with an estimated enrollment of ∼3,000 patients. Treating clinicians or participants themselves will be notified of potential undiagnosed liver disease with site-specific workflows in place to ensure routine clinical care for definitive case confirmation. Primary outcomes will be SLD and fibrotic liver disease detection rates and positive predictive values within 12 months of AI identification. Pre-specified secondary outcomes will assess diagnostic accuracy against other gold-standard modalities, treatment initiation, time to diagnosis, and impact on other clinical events. Outcomes will be compared against historical usual-care and contemporary below-threshold cohorts.
SCOUT-Echo-AI is a prospective multicenter study evaluating the real-world impact of AI-enabled opportunistic liver disease screening using routine echocardiography.

title: A deep-learning system for dental plaque quantification from disclosed intraoral photographs, validation against clinical plaque scoring.
authors: Eduarda Freitas de Andrade; Karolina Felisberto; Robert Lucas Bonifácio Correia; Jamil Awad Shibli; Mohamed A Hassan
abstract:
To determine whether buccal plaque coverage measured automatically from disclosed intraoral photographs agrees with the Turesky-modified Quigley-Hein plaque index (T-QHPI) scored by calibrated dentists.
Twenty adults were photographed in one frontal and two lateral views after 48 hours without oral hygiene, and a calibrated dentist, blind to the model, scored the T-QHPI on the same teeth. Two U-Net (ResNet-34) models, one per view, were trained under participant-level five-fold cross-validation, and coverage was the stained percentage of each outlined buccal crown. Coverage was compared with the clinical grade by Spearman's ρ and, after conversion to T-QHPI grades under index-definition and calibrated thresholds, by weighted κ; participant means by Pearson's r, the intraclass correlation coefficient ICC(2,1) and Bland-Altman analysis.
438 teeth were compared with the clinical grade. Segmentation Dice was 0.88 in both views. Coverage ranked teeth with the clinical index at ρ = 0.856 (95% CI 0.821 to 0.877). After calibration, weighted κ was 0.812 (0.766 to 0.844) against 0.791 (0.710 to 0.853) between two examiners, and agreement within one grade was 96.8%. Participant means correlated at r = 0.930, with ICC(2,1) 0.916.
Automated buccal plaque coverage from disclosed photographs agreed with the T-QHPI scored by a calibrated examiner, and after threshold calibration the agreement did not differ from that between two examiners.
Automated plaque grading from disclosed photographs could serve as an auxiliary tool, a second opinion that supports, rather than replaces, the clinician's plaque scoring, pending external validation.

authors: Katane Elizabeth Kekana; Thokozani Isaac Mtshali
journal: Journal of Education and Learning Technology
abstract: Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.

title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
authors: Muhammad Nur Hudha; Riezky Maya Probosari; Annisa Nur Khasanah; Supurwoko; Salsabila Kholifahtun Nisa’; Gifran Rihla Gifarka Latief
journal: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science
abstract: Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored. Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes. Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement. Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization. Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.

abstract: In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.
