title: Imaging-derived coronary fractional flow reserve: advances in physics-based, machine learning, and physics-informed methods
authors: Tanxin Zhu; Emran Hossen; Chen Zhao; Jingfeng Jiang; Michele Esposito; Jiguang Sun; Weihua Zhou
abstract: Purpose of Review: Imaging-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR) is rapidly evolving beyond conventional computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-based pipelines toward machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and physics-informed approaches that enable fast, wire-free, and scalable functional assessment of coronary artery stenosis. This review synthesizes recent advances in computed tomography (CT)- and angiography-based FFR measurement, with particular emphasis on emerging physics-informed neural networks and neural operators (PINNs and PINOs), as well as key considerations for their clinical translation. Recent Findings: ML/DL approaches have markedly improved automation and computational speed, enabling prediction of pressure and FFR from anatomical descriptors or angiographic contrast dynamics. However, their real-world performance and generalizability can remain variable and sensitive to domain shift, due to multi-center heterogeneity, interpretability challenges, and differences in acquisition protocols and image quality. Physics-informed learning introduces conservation structure and boundary-condition consistency into model training, improving generalizability and reducing dependence on dense supervision while maintaining rapid inference. Recent evaluation trends increasingly highlight deployment-oriented metrics, including calibration, uncertainty quantification, and quality-control gatekeeping, as essential for safe clinical use. Summary: The field is converging toward imaging-derived FFR methods that are faster, more automated, and more reliable. While ML/DL offers substantial efficiency gains, physics-informed frameworks such as PINNs and PINOs may provide a more robust balance between speed and physical consistency. Prospective multi-center validation and standardized evaluation will be critical to support broad and safe clinical adoption.

title: Recent achievements of the National Center Biobank Network (NCBN) bioresources through Japanese fiscal year 2025
authors: Yosuke Omae; Katsushi Tokunaga
abstract: The National Center Biobank Network (NCBN) is constituted by a network of biobanks from five National Centers and the Japan Institute for Health Security (JIHS). The NCBN primarily collects samples from patients with various diseases, amassing a total of more than 250,000 participants and 800,000 human biospecimens as of the end of March 2026. The primary sample types are blood and DNA, with spinal fluid and frozen tissue samples also collected depending on the characteristics of the disease. These samples are accompanied by highly specialized and traceable clinical information supported by advanced medical care and expertise. Moreover, some samples are accompanied by whole-genome sequencing data. Consequently, these resources provide a unique platform for translational research, biomarker discovery, and genomic medicine in Japan. In the present review, we provide a detailed account of the recent achievements of NCBN biobanks and their biospecimens and genomic data.

title: HRC Research Day 2026
abstract: Psychiatry in Malaysia is expanding within a complex training ecosystem that includes university pathways, service-based Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH) training, and the MRCPsych parallel pathway, yet it still lacks a dedicated college under the Academy of Medicine of Malaysia (AMM).This study examined whether regional psychiatry college models and Malaysian workforce evidence support the case for such a platform.A structured narrative comparative review was conducted using bibliographic sources, official institutional websites, targeted Google site-specific searches, and citation tracking.Included sources were organised into a comparative framework matrix and synthesised thematically across governance, training, credentialing, continuing professional development, standards, advocacy, professional identity and international linkage.The review included 11 regional institutional sources and 3 Malaysian contextual documents or data sources.Regional models differed in structure but converged in key functions including training support, credentialing, continuing professional development, standards work, advocacy, professional identity, and selective international linkage.Official Malaysian data identified 111 current pathwaylinked psychiatrists and 445 psychiatrists in MOH settings, indicating that the pathway-linked cohort constituted approximately 24.9% of the MOH psychiatry workforce.Regional psychiatry bodies differ in form but converge in function.Malaysia now has a visible and institutionally relevant psychiatry constituency, suggesting that a future College of Psychiatrists under AMM may be timely as a durable academic-professional platform to strengthen specialty development, rather than as a parallel regulator.

title: Association between maternal antimony exposure and offspring congenital heart defects: findings from a large birth cohort study
authors: Yawen Shao; Lei Cao; Ru Lin; Jie Ran; Qing Liu; Baohong Mao
abstract: Background This nested case–control study aimed to investigate the association between maternal blood antimony concentrations and the risk of congenital heart defects (CHDs) in offspring, identify potential risk factors for CHDs, and inform prevention strategies. Method The study was conducted within a birth cohort established jointly by Gansu Provincial Maternity and Child Care Hospital and Yale University. A total of 291 women were enrolled, including 97 women who gave birth to infants with CHDs (case group) and 194 controls. Controls were selected from the same cohort using a 1:2 matching ratio and matched to cases by age and community. Maternal whole blood samples were collected during prenatal hospitalization before delivery, and antimony concentrations were measured by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to determine an antimony exposure cutoff and classify participants into high and low exposure groups. Conditional multivariable logistic regression was performed to assess the association between maternal blood antimony concentrations and the risk of CHDs in offspring. Results The mean maternal blood antimony concentration was 13.05 μg/L in the control group and 20.30 μg/L in the CHDs group, and the difference between the two groups was statistically significant. Compared with the low exposure group, the high exposure group was associated with a significantly higher risk of CHDs in offspring (OR = 4.455, 95% CI: 2.029–9.782). Similar associations were observed for the subgroups of isolated CHDs, great arteries malformation, septal defects, and atrial septal defects (ASDs). For each 6 μg/L increment in maternal blood antimony, a 38.9% higher risk of CHDs in offspring (OR = 1.389, 95% CI: 1.110–1.735), with consistent findings in the isolated CHDs, septal defects, and ASDs subgroups. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis showed that when maternal blood antimony exceeded 18.409 μg/L, CHDs risk in offspring increased with rising antimony levels. Conclusion Higher maternal blood antimony concentrations were associated with an increased risk of CHDs in offspring. These findings suggest that the prenatal living environment may be a modifiable target for CHD prevention and warrant efforts to minimize exposure to potential environmental sources of antimony.

title: HEART Score as a Predictor of Angiographic Severity of Coronary Artery Disease in Patients Diagnosed with Acute Coronary Syndrome
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Background: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide.Rapid risk stratification of patients presenting with chest pain is essential for early diagnosis and appropriate management.The HEART score, which incorporates History, Electrocardiogram, Age, Risk factors, and Troponin levels, has emerged as a simple and effective clinical tool for predicting major adverse cardiac events.However, limited studies have evaluated its relationship with the angiographic severity of coronary artery disease (CAD), particularly in the Indian population.Objective: To assess the HEART score in patients with acute coronary syndrome and to evaluate its correlation with the angiographic severity of coronary artery disease.Methods: This prospective observational study was conducted in the Department of General Medicine at a tertiary care teaching hospital.A total of 50 adult patients diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome were included.Clinical history, cardiovascular risk factors, electrocardiographic findings, and troponin levels were recorded, and the HEART score was calculated for each patient.Patients were categorized into low-risk (0-3), moderate-risk (4-6), and high-risk (7-10) groups.All patients underwent coronary angiography to determine the severity of coronary artery disease.Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS software, and the association between HEART score categories and angiographic findings was analyzed using the Chi-square test, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant.Results: The mean age of the study population was 56.8 ± 11.4 years, and 68% of the patients were male.Hypertension (60%) and diabetes mellitus (52%) were the most common cardiovascular risk factors.Based on the HEART score classification, 18% of patients were categorized as low risk, 52% as moderate risk, and 30% as high risk.Coronary angiography revealed single vessel disease in 36% of patients, double vessel disease in 26%, triple vessel disease in 20%, and normal coronary arteries in 18%.A significant association was observed between increasing HEART score categories and the severity of coronary artery disease (χ² = 12.84, p = 0.002), with multi-vessel disease predominantly observed in patients with higher HEART scores. Conclusion:The HEART score is a simple and effective bedside risk stratification tool that correlates significantly with the angiographic severity of coronary artery disease in patients with acute coronary syndrome.Its routine use in clinical practice may help identify high-risk patients early and facilitate timely diagnostic and therapeutic interventions.

title: Remnant-cholesterol-inflammatory-index as a novel predictor of cardiometabolic risk and cardiovascular mortality in elderly patients with severe aortic stenosis
authors: Annamaria Mazzone; Melania Gaggini; Ilenia Foffa; Serena Del Turco; Fabrizio Minichilli; Sergio Berti; Cristina Vassalle
abstract: Background Inflammaging activates a vicious cycle common to the progression of structural cardiovascular alterations, cardiometabolic diseases as well as degenerative aortic stenosis (AoS). The remnant cholesterol inflammatory index (RCII) is a new recently proposed biomarker that combines remnant cholesterol and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, resembling inflammaging. However, the role of RCII in terms of cardiometabolic risk and cardiovascular mortality in AoS elderly patients has not been evaluated still now. Aim to assess the association between RCII and cardiovascular risk factors and mortality in AoS elderly patients. Results RCII levels correlated with systemic inflammation biomarkers (closer correlation with interleukin-6), glucose, creatinine, vascular endothelial growth factor and frailty in AoS patients. Inverse correlations were observed with albumin (typically reduced in inflammatory states) and with HDL concentration. The Kaplan-Meier survival estimates showed significantly worse survival in patients with elevated RCII levels (p<0.01) (mean follow-up 19 ± 4 months). In an exploratory multivariable Cox analysis, higher RCII was associated with cardiovascular mortality (HR = 3.5, 95% CI: 1.0–12.0). Conclusion RCII is associated with cardiometabolic risk and adverse prognosis in elderly patients with AoS, providing an additional perspective on the prognostic implications of the coexistence of lipid abnormalities and low-grade inflammation in this population. However, the limited number of cardiovascular deaths warrants cautious interpretation of this estimate. Moreover, external validation, standardized thresholds, serial measurements, and comparison with established risk models are needed before RCII clinical implementation.

title: Extrusion‐Based Bioprinting of Living Bioinks for Tissue and Organ Engineering
authors: Eric Silberman; Elisheva Baruch; Roni Cohen; Assaf Shapira; Tal Dvir
abstract: ABSTRACT Recapitulating the structural complexity of native tissues is a central challenge in tissue engineering, as tissue architecture critically influences cellular maturation and physiological function. Among 3D bioprinting technologies, extrusion‐based bioprinting (EBB) has emerged as the predominant platform for fabricating complex, heterogeneous, and large‐scale tissues, despite inherent limitations in printing speed and resolution. In this review, we examine the defining advantage underlying EBB's widespread adoption: its exceptional versatility. We discuss the broad range of living bioinks and biomaterial inks compatible with extrusion, emphasizing the ease with which multiple materials and cell populations can be integrated within a single construct. We then examine how support matrices and advanced printhead geometries have expanded the accessible material and architectural space, enabling the fabrication of soft, freeform, anisotropic, and multicompartment tissues. We critically evaluate the fundamental physical constraints of extrusion, particularly the tradeoff between printing resolution and cell‐damaging shear stress, and highlight strategies that transform these limitations into new biofabrication capabilities. Finally, we identify 4D bioprinting, high‐speed fabrication, and in situ bioprinting as three emerging frontiers that may define the next generation of EBB for tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.

title: Activation of perivascular thermogenic fat improves aortic stenosis
authors: Staffan Hildebrand; Klaus Wunderling; Zuzanna Siwik-Rog; Alexander SCHMIDT; Jorge A. Barrero; Nicolás Gómez-Banoy; Laia Reverte-Salisa; Benjamin Freyter; Sebastian Zimmer; Georg Nickenig; Paul Cohen; Alexander Pfeifer
abstract: Aim: Aortic stenosis (AS) is a common condition with exponential increases in incidence in aging populations. Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) forms the outer layer of the aortic wall and has - especially in the thoracic area - characteristics of thermogenic adipose tissue, which dissipates energy and releases endocrine factors. Here, we set out to investigate the role of thermogenic PVAT in AS. Methods and results: We studied the role of (PVAT) in the development of AS in a murine model of AS. To specifically delineate the role of PVAT activity in AS, we used a pharmacological β3-adrenergic agonist as well as cold exposure in combination with a genetic mouse model with deficient PVAT development. To investigate the role of thermogenic adipose tissue in human AS, we used 18F-FDG PET-CT imaging. We found that pharmacological activation of thermogenic adipose tissue resulted in an improvement of AS, but not in mice genetically deficient in PVAT. Similarly, PVAT was found to be protective against AS during physiological stimulation of PVAT using cold exposure. Mechanistically, PVAT activation resulted in enhanced aortic distensibility and cellular remodeling of the aortic wall, possibly via release of polyunsaturated fatty acids and oxylipins from perivascular adipocytes. Finally, analysis of thermogenic fat activity in humans revealed that mediastinal thermogenic fat activity correlated negatively with diagnostic criteria of AS severity, suggesting an important role for PVAT activity in human AS. Conclusion: Our data indicate that PVAT activation reduces aortic stenosis and supports aortic remodeling to improve ascending aorta hemodynamics. PVAT activation might be a novel therapeutic target to ameliorate AS progression. Translational perspective: Currently, there are no effective strategies for treating AS other than valve replacement. Since the molecular mechanisms underlying the disease progression remain unclear, there are no pharmacological agents approved for either treatment or prevention of this disease. Furthermore, AS development cannot currently be predicted and is often only diagnosed when patients develop symptoms, which may be 10-20 years after disease onset. Therefore, identifying novel mechanisms that improve aortic valve function and prevent AS is of high medical need. This study identifies activation of PVAT-dependent aortic remodeling as a potential new therapeutic approach to improve or prevent AS.

title: The Safety and Efficacy of Intravascular Lithotripsy in Treating Calcified Peripheral Arterial Disease
authors: Ahmed Aljawadi; Saqib Ashraf
abstract: Calcified peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a common health condition associated with increased morbidity and mortality.Endovascular procedures have become more common in treating these lesions, and plain balloon angioplasty (PBA) is often used for vessels with mild-to-moderate calcification.However, decreased vascular compliance in heavily calcified vessels leads to poorer outcomes and higher complication risk.Intravascular shockwave lithotripsy is a more novel endovascular management option.It uses a specially designed balloon catheter to create shockwaves in an attempt to modify and increase compliance of the calcified plaque.This review aims to assess the safety profile and efficacy of intravascular lithotripsy (IVL).The currently available literature shows that use of IVL for calcified PAD has a good safety profile and low complication rate.Intravascular lithotripsy has also been shown to be more effective in treating patients with calcified PAD as compared to PBA alone.Whilst short-term and mid-term results are promising, there is a scarcity of published long-term data.Hence, further long-term data is required before a definitive conclusion can be drawn.

title: Expanding role of nuclear medicine in cardiac amyloidosis: insights from the EJNMMI collection
authors: Mahdi Zirakchian Zadeh; Medhat Osman
abstract: Recent advances in nuclear medicine are reshaping the evaluation of cardiac amyloidosis, as highlighted by the recent collection published in EJNMMI (collection link: https://link.springer.com/collections/igfdhcddjg). This commentary summarizes key insights from these studies, emphasizing the evolving shift from conventional diagnostic imaging toward a more integrated and comprehensive approach. Emerging developments include novel amyloid PET tracers, improved diagnostic accuracy with SPECT/CT, multimodality imaging strategies, and enhanced assessment of systemic disease burden extending beyond the left ventricle. There is also growing interest in longitudinal monitoring, pre-symptomatic detection, and the role of artificial intelligence. Together, these advances position nuclear medicine as an essential tool for disease characterization, risk stratification, and treatment assessment.

title: LIPOPROTEÍNA(A) NA ESTRATIFICAÇÃO DO RISCO CARDIOVASCULAR: FUNDAMENTOS, RECOMENDAÇÕES DA DIRETRIZ BRASILEIRA DE DISLIPIDEMIAS 2025 E PERSPECTIVAS TERAPÊUTICAS
authors: Antonio Henrique Lima Rodrigues; PIETRO VALADARES REZENDE NUNES; Isabella Neife Alves Sary Eldin; Mariana Brun de Oliveira
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: A lipoproteína(a) [Lp(a)] é uma partícula semelhante à lipoproteína de baixa densidade (LDL), na qual a apolipoproteína B-100 se liga à apolipoproteína(a), proteína homóloga ao plasminogênio. Suas concentrações são determinadas em mais de 90% pelo gene LPA, mantêm-se estáveis ao longo da vida e não respondem à dieta, ao exercício ou às estatinas. Estudos epidemiológicos e genéticos estabeleceram a Lp(a) como fator de risco causal, contínuo e independente para doença cardiovascular aterosclerótica e estenose valvar aórtica. Esta revisão narrativa, baseada na PubMed/MEDLINE e em documentos oficiais, descreve os fundamentos biológicos e epidemiológicos da Lp(a), analisa as recomendações da Diretriz Brasileira de Dislipidemias e Prevenção da Aterosclerose de 2025 e discute as perspectivas terapêuticas. A diretriz recomenda dosar a Lp(a) uma vez na vida em todos os adultos, preferencialmente por ensaio independente da isoforma, em nmol/L. Valores ≥ 50 mg/dL (≥ 125 nmol/L) passam a ser agravante de risco, capaz de elevar a categoria de baixo para intermediário ou de intermediário para alto, e níveis acima de 180 mg/dL (390 nmol/L) indicam alto risco; recomenda-se também a investigação familiar em cascata. Sem terapia específica aprovada, o manejo apoia-se no controle intensivo do LDL-colesterol e dos fatores de risco. Os inibidores de PCSK9 reduzem a Lp(a) em 20 a 30%, e terapias silenciadoras de RNA e inibidores orais alcançam reduções de 80% a mais de 95%. Em 2026, porém, o pelacarsena não reduziu eventos no estudo Lp(a)HORIZON, o que torna decisivos os ensaios em andamento com RNA de interferência.

title: Time-aligned segmental strain as a diagnostic marker for obstructive coronary artery disease in patients with chronic chest pain
authors: Assami Rösner; Hatice Akay Caglayan; Mehran Jazbani; Semra Oztemel Sari; Pablo Marti Castellote; Didrik Kjønås; Sandro Queirós
abstract: BACKGROUND: Myocardial strain curves provide valuable insights into coronary artery disease (CAD) beyond conventional peak strain measurements. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic utility of time-aligned segmental strain and strain rate (S/SR) curves to identify obstructive CAD in consecutive chest pain patients. METHODS: A total of 510 chest-pain patients referred to coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) were included. Segmental strain curves were time-aligned using aortic valve closure (AVC) and cardiac cycle length as reference points. Average S/SR curves were generated for 18 myocardial segments, establishing reference curves from a group of 314 chronic chest-pain patients without CAD (No-CAD). Deviations were defined based on thresholds of peak S/SR or average S/SR curve deviation over systole and the first half of diastole. RESULTS: Significant differences were observed between groups, particularly between the revascularized MI, CABG, or 3-vessel CAD groups compared to the No-CAD group (p<0.05). ROC curve analysis demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance for CABG patients (AUC up to 0.933), while the detection rate for PCI was limited (AUC < 0.7). Global longitudinal strain rate in early diastole (GLSR E) and segmental peak SR E showed the highest diagnostic accuracy. These findings confirm that time-aligned strain analysis improves the detection of significant CAD but remains limited for identifying patients with mild disease. CONCLUSION: Time-aligned segmental strain analysis improved detection of high-grade disease requiring CABG but could not distinguish single-vessel from non-obstructive CAD. Pathological strain patterns became significant only in advanced CAD, indicating that segmental resting strain analysis has clinical utility primarily for identifying advanced CAD.

title: Prognostic value of the ECG strain pattern in aortic stenosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Yara El Deghel; Tony John Azizi
abstract: Review title: Prognostic value of the ECG strain pattern in aortic stenosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis Type and method of review: Meta analysis Stage of review at time of this submission: Review ongoing — the protocol has been finalised and the peer-reviewed search prepared; formal screening not yet started. Review question: In Adults with aortic stenosis, what is the effect of ECG left ventricular strain pattern compared with No ECG strain pattern on All-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events (including aortic valve replacement)? Searches: The following sources will be searched: Europe PMC (PubMed, MEDLINE & preprints), PubMed / MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection. Additional records may be imported from other databases. No date or language restrictions are applied unless otherwise stated. The search strategy underwent peer review (PRESS) before execution. Condition or domain being studied: Adults with aortic stenosis Participants / population: Adults with aortic stenosis Intervention(s), exposure(s): ECG left ventricular strain pattern Comparator(s) / control: No ECG strain pattern Types of study to be included: Inclusion criteria: Adults with aortic stenosis; ECG strain pattern defined; Reports hazard ratios or event data for mortality or MACE; Prospective or retrospective cohort studies; Full-text article published in English. Exclusion criteria: No outcome follow-up; Strain assessed only by echocardiography (speckle-tracking); Reviews, editorials, letters or conference abstracts; Overlapping cohorts (the largest or most recent report is kept) Main outcome(s): All-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events (including aortic valve replacement) Data extraction (selection and coding): Two reviewers will independently screen titles/abstracts and full texts, blinded to each other’s decisions, and extract data in duplicate using a standardised, piloted form. Disagreements will be resolved by discussion or a third reviewer. Risk of bias (quality) assessment: The risk of bias of each included study will be assessed independently by two reviewers using a study-design-appropriate tool. Disagreements will be resolved by consensus. Risk of bias in the review itself will be appraised with ROBIS. Strategy for data synthesis: Results will be synthesised narratively. Where studies are sufficiently homogeneous, effect estimates will be pooled in a meta-analysis using a fixed- or random-effects model as indicated by heterogeneity (I²). The certainty of the evidence will be rated using GRADE.

title: Isolated Disturbance of Consciousness as Initial Presentation of Staphylococcus aureus Endocarditis: A Case Report With Brief Literature Review
authors: Weixiong Zhong; 黄珊珊; Jing Jiang; Zhixu Tan
abstract: Objective:Challenging differential diagnosis Background:Infective endocarditis (IE) typically presents with fever, a heart murmur, or constitutional symptoms, making diagnosis challenging when neurological manifestations predominate.We report an atypical case of IE in which disturbance of consciousness was the initial manifestation. Case Report:A man in his 50s was admitted to our hospital with isolated disturbance of consciousness and no history of fever; a temperature of 38 °C was recorded on admission.Investigations confirmed an extensive acute right hemispheric watershed (border-zone) infarction involving the right temporoparietal lobe, without evidence of hemorrhagic transformation or intracranial hemorrhage.Subsequent workup identified Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia, mitral valve vegetation, and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome.The absence of classic IE risk factors contributed to a delayed diagnosis.Guideline-concordant clinical management was implemented.Long-term outcome data were unavailable because of patient transfer; only in-hospital mortality (after transfer) was confirmed.We discuss the application of the 2023 Duke criteria to this case and examine factors contributing to the delayed diagnosis of IE.Disturbance of consciousness as the predominant initial manifestation of S. aureus IE is rare and frequently results in diagnostic delay.This case underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for IE in patients with sepsis complicated by acute cerebral infarction, particularly among critical care and neurology clinicians. Conclusions:This case highlights isolated disturbance of consciousness as an atypical initial presentation of IE.Although IE is frequently complicated by acute cerebral infarction, clinicians may not routinely consider IE in the differential diagnosis of patients presenting with disturbed consciousness.

title: Comparative genomics identifies a cyl-like region in Streptococcus sinensis isolates from a patient with infective endocarditis
authors: Wei Ma; Yanjun Zhang; 黄晓春; Yuxiang Wan; Changzi Deng; Jia Lin; Li Xu; Qin Qin
abstract: Streptococcus sinensis is an uncommon member of the viridans group streptococci reported in infective endocarditis (IE), but its genomic characteristics remain incompletely defined. We performed whole-genome sequencing of three S. sinensis isolates recovered from blood culture and valvular tissue from a single patient with IE and compared them with 199 public Streptococcus genomes. Orthology analysis, phylogenetic reconstruction, SNP analysis, VFDB and CARD screening, gene-specific BLAST, Pfam/HMMER analysis, read mapping, synteny comparison, in silico structural modeling, and erythrocyte hemolysis assays were integrated. The three isolates differed by only 0–1 SNPs and formed a near-clonal group. Core single-copy ortholog phylogeny placed S. sinensis closest to S. cristatus , followed by S. sanguinis and S. gordonii . The three isolates retained the host-interaction-associated genes eno , pavA , and plr / gapA and carried an identical 11,341-bp, 12-gene cyl -like block comprising 11 cyl -like genes and acpC . Core-gene phylogeny analysis indicated that the distribution of the complete block was lineage-associated. Gene-specific BLAST and read mapping confirmed full-length sequence conservation and complete mapped-base coverage of the block, while Pfam/HMMER supported enzyme- and transporter-associated domain assignments for several encoded proteins. Structural modeling predicted soluble enzyme-like folds for CylG-like and CylZ-like proteins and a membrane-permease-like architecture with transmembrane helices for CylB-like. On Columbia sheep-blood agar, all three clinical isolates showed visible hemolytic zones and exhibited detectable hemolytic activity in a sheep erythrocyte hemolysis assay. All three S. sinensis isolates shared a type 1 CARD-derived resistance-marker profile containing only Spne_parC_FLO . These findings clarify the phylogenomic position of the near-clonal clinical isolates and identify a shared cyl -like genomic region accompanied by measurable hemolytic activity, providing a basis for further investigation of their host-interaction and pathogenic potential.

title: Mitral valve repair for pediatric dilated cardiomyopathy with severe functional mitral regurgitation: a mechanism-anchored, proof-of-concept preoperative selection framework with supportive cohort and pooled outcomes
authors: Mete Han Kızılkaya; Boran Cakan; Aylin Ardali; Mehmet Biçer; Murat Tanyıldız; Ömer Özden; Ender Ödemiş
abstract: Functional mitral regurgitation (FMR) develops in 40–65% of children with dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and independently predicts death or transplantation. Published pediatric mitral valve repair (MVR) series from 2003 to 2024 report clinical stabilization rates of 0% to 100% and perioperative mortality of 0% to 50%. This heterogeneity is multifactorial, reflecting the surgical era, technique, institutional experience, patient acuity, and reporting standards, with patient selection being a contributing factor that has not yet been systematically examined. No preoperative framework currently exists to identify which children are most likely to benefit. A mechanism-anchored, three-category proof-of-concept clinical framework was defined a priori. Patients were classified as Non-MR-dominant if any of four affirmative features were documented (N1: toxic, storage, infiltrative, or myopathic etiology; N2: primary structural mitral valve disease; N3: preoperative irreversible end-organ failure or ECMO with multi-organ dysfunction; N4: severe RV dysfunction, fixed pulmonary hypertension, or severe tricuspid regurgitation from RV/annular dilatation). Patients without any N-feature who met three volume-overload criteria (idiopathic, familial, or sarcomeric DCM; functional MR ≥ 3+; LVEDd Pettersen Z-score ≥ + 5) were classified as MR-dominant. A Borderline MR-dominant category captured patients who did not meet all MR-dominant criteria but satisfied one of three predefined conditions (infancy with intermediate fractional shortening; post-myocarditis with documented regional scar or fibrotic substrate; or an LVEDd Pettersen Z-score of + 3.5 to < + 5 with severe functional MR). The framework was applied to a single-center cohort of six consecutive children and, masked to outcome, to all 22 previously published pediatric MVR-receiving patients. In the index cohort, three MR-dominant children underwent MVR and sustained remodeling, with transplant-free survival at a median 30-month follow-up and NT-proBNP reductions of 86–99%. Three children not selected for MVR (an MR-dominant child whose family declined surgery, and two Non-MR-dominant children) all died. In the pooled MVR-receiving cohort ( n = 25), MR-dominant plus Borderline patients achieved clinical stabilization and/or remodeling in 16/20 (80%) versus 1/5 (20%) Non-MR-dominant patients (Fisher exact p = 0.024; odds ratio 11.0, 95% CI 1.3–91.8). The association is statistically significant in the primary specification but is fragile to single-patient reclassification, an unavoidable consequence of reporting only five Non-MR-dominant patients across three decades of global pediatric literature. A fully preoperative, mechanism-anchored framework that places the burden of proof on Non-MR-dominant assignment offers a coherent, biologically grounded interpretation of three decades of heterogeneous pediatric MVR outcomes. In MR-dominant disease, MVR may support clinical stabilization with the potential for remodeling and may be a viable bridging or alternative strategy where transplantation and durable ventricular assist device support are inaccessible. The framework should be regarded as a proof-of-concept clinical hypothesis rather than a validated decision algorithm; prospective multicenter validation is required before clinical adoption.

title: A Rare Case of Gorlin-Goltz Syndrome with Multiple Basal Cell Carcinoma Lesions: A Multidisciplinary Surgical Approach
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Background: Gorlin-Goltz Syndrome, also known as nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome (NBCCS), is a rare autosomal dominant disorder marked by multiple basal cell carcinomas (BCCs), odontogenic keratocysts, and systemic skeletal anomalies.Early diagnosis is crucial due to the syndrome's potential for multisystem involvement and malignancy risk.This case aims to highlight the clinical spectrum, diagnostic evaluation, and surgical management strategies in a patient with recurrent BCCs in the context of Gorlin syndrome, while emphasizing the role of multidisciplinary care in optimizing outcomes. Clinical Presentation:A case of a 40-year-old Indian male presenting with multiple cutaneous lesions, including ulcerated pigmented nodules, predominantly on the scalp, limbs, and torso.He had a prior history of basal cell carcinoma excisions and a superficial parotidectomy with neck dissection.Systemic evaluation revealed hallmark features of Gorlin syndrome: macrocephaly, frontal bossing, odontogenic keratocysts (on orthopantomogram), and calcification of the falx cerebri (on CECT brain).Wide local excision (WLE) was performed for a symptomatic ulcerated lesion on the left hand.Histopathology confirmed recurrence of BCC.No systemic metastasis or skeletal anomalies were noted, though mild pulmonary arterial hypertension was detected on echocardiography. Conclusion:The case highlights the importance of early recognition and comprehensive management in Gorlin-Goltz syndrome.Multidisciplinary surgical intervention, supported by regular follow-up and systemic evaluation, is essential to prevent complications and recurrence.The case adds to the scarce literature on Indian presentations of Gorlin syndrome and reinforces the need for genetic counselling and vigilant long-term care.

title: Clinical Symptom Burden and Its Association With Echocardiographic Parameters and Comorbidities in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Retrospective Study
authors: Reena A Athisivam; Venkkatesh Nagajothi Shanmugasundaram; Syed Abrar Hasan Syed Javid Hasan; Mohit Kumar Ramkumar; Neha V Damodar; Neeharikka Gopalakrishnan; Deviabhirami N S; Horavaasan H; Hari Vishak Pandian Jeyamurugan; Hariharan Srinivasan
abstract: Introduction: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome in which substantial symptoms may occur despite preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF).Echocardiographic abnormalities involving ventricular filling, left atrial remodeling, diastolic function, and pulmonary pressures may contribute to symptom burden.This study evaluated the association between clinical symptom severity, echocardiographic parameters, and comorbidities in patients with HFpEF.Study: This retrospective observational cross-sectional study was conducted at the Government Peripheral Hospital, Periyar Nagar, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, from March 2025 to March 2026.A total of 216 patients aged ≥18 years with HFpEF and LVEF ≥50% were included.Clinical symptom burden was assessed using New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class and categorized as I-II or III-IV.Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, and echocardiographic parameters, including LVEF, left ventricular mass, left atrial volume index (LAVI), E/e′ ratio, diastolic dysfunction grade, and estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP), were evaluated.Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with NYHA III-IV symptoms.Results: The mean age was 67.8 ± 10.4 years, and 53.7% were female.Hypertension was the most prevalent comorbidity (80.6%), while 76.9% had ≥2 major comorbidities.Fifty-five patients (25.5%) had NYHA III-IV symptoms.Compared with NYHA I-II, the severe symptom group had higher E/e′ (17.4 ± 5.0 vs. 12.6 ± 4.0), LAVI (44.5 ± 12.1 vs. 34.2± 9.1 mL/m²), LV mass, and PASP (43.9 ± 12.4 vs. 36.8± 8.7 mmHg), with significantly more advanced diastolic dysfunction.On multivariable analysis, E/e′ (adjusted OR 1.18), LAVI (adjusted OR 1.05), and PASP (adjusted OR 1.04) were independently associated with severe symptoms.Conclusion: Symptom severity in HFpEF was associated more strongly with abnormal filling pressures, left atrial remodeling, and pulmonary hemodynamics than with preserved systolic function alone.E/e′, LAVI, and PASP may provide useful complementary markers of symptomatic burden and support a multidimensional echocardiographic assessment of HFpEF.

title: Morphological Study of the Tricuspid Valve in Human Embalmed Hearts
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Background: The tricuspid valve, situated between the right atrium and right ventricle, is a vital component of cardiac anatomy whose morphological variability has significant implications for surgical and interventional cardiac procedures.Anatomical knowledge of its three leaflets-anterior, posterior, and septal-is indispensable for effective valve repair, prosthetic valve design, and understanding functional tricuspid regurgitation.Aims & Objectives: To measure and compare the annular circumference, leaflet length, and leaflet height of the anterior, posterior, and septal leaflets of the tricuspid valve in human embalmed cadaveric hearts, and to establish normative morphometric data relevant to clinical and surgical practice. Materials and Methods:A descriptive cross-sectional anatomical study was conducted at Father Muller Medical College, Mangalore, Karnataka, on 50 embalmed human cadaveric hearts.Annular circumference, valve diameter, and the length and height of each leaflet were measured using a thread-and-scale method and measuring tape.Descriptive statistics including mean, standard deviation, and range were calculated for all parameters.Results: The annular circumference ranged from 8.9 to 15.3 cm (mean ± SD: 11.84 ± 1.42 cm) and valve diameter from 2.83 to 4.87 cm (mean: 3.75 ± 0.48 cm).The anterior leaflet was consistently the largest with a mean length of 4.82 ± 0.83 cm and height of 2.04 ± 0.23 cm.The septal leaflet showed intermediate dimensions, while the posterior leaflet was the smallest and most variable.Conclusion: Significant morphometric variability exists in the tricuspid valve across cadaveric specimens.The anterior leaflet was the largest in all measured parameters, while the posterior leaflet demonstrated the greatest variability.These findings provide normative data of practical value for cardiac surgeons, interventional cardiologists, and biomedical engineers involved in prosthetic valve design.

title: Severe Rheumatic Mitral Stenosis With Multivalvular Abnormalities in a British-Born Adult Without a Recognized History of Acute Rheumatic Fever
authors: Adel Kenawi; Hatem Ali Abdelnasser; Nouralhuda Hamad; Marwa Ruziek; Ahmed Jaber
abstract: Rheumatic heart disease (RHD) has become uncommon in the United Kingdom, particularly among Britishborn adults without a recognized history of acute rheumatic fever (ARF).A 40-year-old British-born female with no previously diagnosed cardiac disease presented with a one-year history of progressive exertional dyspnoea.Chest radiography demonstrated cardiomegaly, and the N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide concentration was 1,800 pg/mL.Transthoracic echocardiography showed very severe mitral stenosis with characteristic rheumatic morphology, a mitral valve area of 0.33 cm² by planimetry, and a mean transmitral gradient of 16.6 mmHg.Associated findings included mild mitral regurgitation, tricuspid valve abnormalities with moderate-tosevere tricuspid regurgitation, and discordant aortic valve findings consistent with a low-flow, low-gradient pattern of aortic stenosis, an estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure of approximately 105-110 mmHg, left ventricular systolic impairment, and impaired right ventricular longitudinal systolic function.Further history identified intermittent involuntary left-hand movements, arthralgia, and an annular abdominal eruption with central pallor.These features raised the possibility of previously unrecognized rheumatic manifestations but were insufficient to establish the diagnosis of ARF.Following transoesophageal echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, and multidisciplinary review, the patient underwent mitral and aortic valve replacement with tricuspid valve repair.This case highlights that advanced RHD can present without a documented history of ARF and emphasizes the importance of valve morphology, integrated haemodynamic assessment, and timely multidisciplinary management.

title: Remimazolam-based total intravenous anesthesia for prone cervical spine surgery in a patient with previously undiagnosed dilated cardiomyopathy after aborted anesthetic induction: A case report
authors: Jooyong Lee; Sanghi Park
abstract: Unexpected hemodynamic deterioration during anesthesia induction may show previously undiagnosed cardiac dysfunction. Herein, we report a case of successful remimazolam-based total intravenous anesthesia in a patient with newly diagnosed dilated cardiomyopathy (DCMP) who underwent prone cervical spine surgery. A 113-kg man with quadriplegia owing to cervical spinal cord injury underwent emergency cervical decompression and fusion surgery. Severe desaturation and hypotension developed despite FiO₂ 1.0 during the initial anesthetic attempt using etomidate and sevoflurane-remifentanil anesthesia, and surgery was aborted. A subsequent evaluation showed DCMP with severely reduced left ventricular systolic function. Reoperation was performed under total intravenous anesthesia with remimazolam–remifentanil. Although transient desaturation and reduced tidal volume developed after prone positioning, surgery was completed with relatively stable hemodynamics. In conclusion, remimazolam-based total intravenous anesthesia may be useful in selected high-risk patients with severe left ventricular dysfunction.

title: Effects of violet light exposure on aging dogs: a pilot study
authors: Kana MIYAMOTO; Nanami Ono; Shinichiro Kondo; Yukihiro Miwa; Kazuo Tsubota; Makiko Ozawa; Takefumi Kikusui
abstract: Aging in dogs is known to induce various physical and brain alterations similar to dementia in humans. Concurrently with the recent extension of canine life expectancy, these age-related changes have imposed growing burdens on both dogs and their owners, emerging as a significant social issue. However, no curative treatment has yet been established, and the current mainstay of management focuses on improving the quality of life through symptomatic therapies, such as environmental modifications and pharmacotherapy. This study focused on violet light, which has suggested efficacy against such age-related changes. We developed a novel violet light irradiation device and evaluated its efficacy and safety in elderly dogs as a pilot study. An intra-individual comparison using an ABA design was employed with geriatric dogs aged 14 to 16 years housed in a senior dog care facility (two of which discontinued midway). The study design consisted of a one-month violet light exposure phase preceded and followed by two-week non-exposure periods. Physical activity levels were measured using accelerometers and cognitive function was assessed using the DISHAA and CCDR. To evaluate the safety, general physical and ophthalmic examinations were conducted by veterinarians. As a result, no significant overall effect was found on activity levels (Daytime: x 2 = 4.22, p = 0.12; Nighttime: x 2 = 1.58, p = 0.45). Similarly, no significant overall effects were observed for either the DISHAA or the CCDR (DISHAA: x 2 = 1.60, p = 0.45; CCDR: x 2 = 1.56, p = 0.46). However, a trend toward cognitive improvement was observed in six out of seven dogs and an upward trend in activity levels-indicating physical function improvement-was noted in two out of seven dogs. Regarding safety, no overt clinical abnormalities associated with violet light irradiation were identified. This pilot study demonstrated no clear overall effect, though some individuals showed signs of improvement. Future research should consider large-scale trials controlling for various variables.

title: Pre-Anesthetic Venous Excess Ultrasound Score for Predicting Spinal Anesthesia-Induced Hypotension in Geriatric Patients Undergoing Elective Lower Body Surgeries: A Prospective Observational Study
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Background: Spinal anesthesia-induced hypotension (SAIH) complications are still prevalent in 16-33% of cases.Objectives: To assess the correlation between the pre-anesthetic venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) grading system and the prediction of SAIH in elderly patients, as well as the correlation between internal jugular vein (IJV) measurements and SAIH prediction in geriatric patients.Methods: This prospective observational investigation included 127 patients aged ≥ 65 years at Tanta University Hospitals over one year.All patients were divided into two groups: Group A (n = 56) with no SAIH and Group B (n = 71) with SAIH.A comprehensive evaluation of prominent systemic veins, including hepatic, portal, renal, and internal jugular veins, was performed on all patients.Results: Delta IJV diameter (ΔIJV-D), delta IJV area (ΔIJV-A), and IJV collapsibility index (IJV-CI) were significantly predictive of hypotension.ΔIJV-D showed an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.697 (P<0.001) at a cutoff >0.11, with 77.46% sensitivity, 57.14% specificity, 69.62% positive predictive value (PPV), and 66.67% negative predictive value (NPV).ΔIJV-A had an AUC of 0.635 (P=0.009) at a cutoff >0.17, with 78.87% sensitivity, 55.36% specificity, 69.14% PPV, and 67.39% NPV.IJV-CI demonstrated an AUC of 0.739 (P<0.001) at a cutoff >19, with 80.28% sensitivity, 76.79% specificity, 81.43% PPV, and 75.44%NPV.Conclusions: Predictors of SAIH in geriatric patients include the simplicity and noninvasiveness of pre-anesthetic IJV-CI, ΔIJV-A, and ΔIJV-D.In contrast, VExUS did not predict SAIH during perioperative assessment.

title: Coronary Artery Disease among Patients Undergoing Valve Replacement Surgery: A Retrospective Study of Angiographic Profiles and Predictors at a Southern Indian Tertiary Care Centre
authors: Gailin Bronson Sebastian; Yokesh Madhavan; Venkatesh Babu; Kiron Sukulal; Jai Arthe; Arya Rajesh; Shreya Gailin; Krishna Viju
journal: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH
abstract: Introduction: Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) frequently co-exists with Valvular Heart Disease (VHD). In developing countries like India, the shifting epidemiology from rheumatic to degenerative VHD alters this association. Concomitant CAD drastically dictates surgical strategies, yet local angiographic profile data remains scarce. Aim: To determine the angiographic profile and clinical predictors of CAD in patients undergoing Coronary Angiography (CAG) prior to valve replacement surgery at an Indian tertiary care centre. Materials and Methods: The present retrospective study was conducted at Sree Mookambika Institute of Medical Sciences, Kanyakumari, Tamil Nadu, South India, and analysed data of 200 consecutive patients undergoing preoperative CAG before valve replacement surgery. Demographic profiles, cardiovascular risk factors, echocardiographic parameters, and angiographic findings were reviewed. Patients were stratified into CAD and non CAD cohorts. Obstructive CAD was defined angiographically. Statistical analysis utilised Chi-square and Student’s t-tests. Results: The cohort’s mean age was 55.6±9.3 years; 127 (63.5%) were males (63.5%). Prevalences of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidaemia, and tobacco use were 71 (35.5%), 64 (32%), 30 (15%), and 15 (7.5%), respectively. Patients with CAD were significantly older (mean age: 59.2±8.5 vs 53.8±9.1 years; p<0.001) and predominantly males (72 (73.5%) vs. 55 (53.9%); p=0.005). Increasing age and diabetes mellitus emerged as independent predictors of CAD in multivariate analysis (OR 1.09, 95% CI 1.05-1.13; p<0.001 and OR 2.49, 95% CI 1.10-5.63; p=0.028, respectively). No statistically significant association was observed between CAD status and valves involved namely, Mitral Valve Disease (MVD), Aortic Valve Disease (AVD) and combined valve disease or valve surgery performed. AVD showed a non significant trend toward higher prevalence in the CAD group (p=0.11). Left Anterior Descending (LAD) artery was the most frequently diseased vessel {49 (50%)}. Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF) was marginally lower in the CAD arm (54.2±12.4% vs 57.1±11.3%; p=0.05), while Atrial Fibrillation (AF) lacked statistical correlation (p=0.89). Conclusion: The CAD in Indian valve replacement candidates was independently associated with advanced age, diabetes mellitus, and standard atherosclerotic risk factors. There was no statistically significant association between presence of CAD and the underlying valve pathology, or the type of surgery performed. Preoperative angiographic screening is critical for precise surgical planning, which should be dictated not only by age but by the presence of cardiovascular risk factors.

title: Translational maturity of artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography varies across cardiovascular diseases
authors: Huanhuan Chen; Jingjuan Huang; Xumin Hou
abstract: Electrocardiography is a widely available and low-cost cardiovascular test, and artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) can identify latent electrical phenotypes beyond conventional interpretation. However, high retrospective discrimination does not necessarily translate into clinically reliable or actionable benefit. This critical narrative review evaluates the translational maturity of AI-ECG across arrhythmias, acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, valvular heart disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and cardiac amyloidosis. PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Web of Science were searched from January 1, 2022, through July 10, 2026, with earlier landmark studies added by backward citation tracking. Seventy-seven publications informed the review. Evidence was appraised using five clinically oriented criteria: intended use, reference-standard reliability, external validation and transportability, clinical actionability, and effects on workflow or patient outcomes. AI-ECG has progressed furthest in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction triage and reduced-left-ventricular-ejection-fraction screening, where prospective or randomized studies have demonstrated workflow or diagnostic-yield benefits, whereas acute myocardial infarction rule-out has reached prospective multicenter diagnostic validation. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy screening has also advanced through international validation and prospective implementation. By contrast, occlusion myocardial infarction detection, prediction of occult or future atrial fibrillation, valvular heart disease, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, long-term heart-failure prediction, and cardiac amyloidosis remain primarily validation-stage or risk-enrichment applications. Across domains, broader adoption is constrained by label quality, calibration, transportability, operating-threshold selection, and limited patient-outcome evidence. AI-ECG is therefore best positioned as clinician-supervised decision support linked to explicit downstream testing and care pathways.

title: Antecedents and consequences of Green-tech FDI in emerging markets
authors: Zhuoran Liu
abstract: As environmental pressures intensify, attracting sustainable foreign direct investment (FDI), particularly green-tech FDI, has become a critical pathway for emerging markets to achieve environmental sustainability. However, existing research remains fragmented, offering limited insights into why green-tech FDI enters emerging markets and how it affects regional green innovation. This thesis addresses these gaps by systematically examining both the antecedents and consequences of green-tech FDI through three empirical studies using regional data from China. Study 1 and Study 2 focus on the antecedents of green-tech FDI. Study 1 examines how host-country conditions can attract green-tech FDI, highlighting the role of environmental management information disclosure (EMID) by domestic firms in reducing information gaps and strengthening green market–seeking motives. Study 2 shifts attention to the active decision-making of green-tech FDI, showing that under uncertainty, green-tech foreign investors engage in identity-based bandwagon learning by imitating peers with similar green identities, thereby mitigating investment risks. Study 3 turns to the consequences of green-tech FDI. It demonstrates that, due to the technological complexity of green innovation and limited absorptive capacity in emerging markets, green-tech FDI may generate crowding-out effects rather than purely positive spillovers. Adopting a network perspective, the study further finds that universities play a key moderating role: through broad linkages and deep collaborations, they help mitigate negative spillovers and facilitate the diffusion of green technologies. Together, the three studies advance the literature on sustainable FDI by differentiating green-tech FDI from general FDI and identifying the specific mechanisms that shape its entry decisions and local innovation outcomes. Practically, the findings provide guidance for emerging-market governments and firms on how to attract and manage sustainable investment, balance growth with environmental objectives, and strengthen local innovation ecosystems.

title: Combating Data and Target Shifts in Visual Tasks
authors: Zhaorui Tan
abstract: The rapid advancement of deep learning models for visual tasks has led to significant progress in many domains. However, a key challenge remains: ensuring that models can generalize effectively to unseen samples or novel classes, especially in real-world scenarios where training data-target pairs are often limited or unavailable, and test data may exhibit shifts in both data and targets. This thesis addresses the problem of shifts across data and targets, proposing novel methods to improve model generalization and transferability in complex settings. The thesis identifies the different shift scenarios for visual tasks and presents their problem forms. The research first relaxes the static target distribution assumption in Multi-Domain Generalization (mDG) tasks, introducing the General Multi-Domain Generalization (GMDG) objective to improve generalization under varying data shifts. Specifically, Extensive experiments validate that GMDG is feasible for classification, segmentation, and regression tasks. Further considering extreme target distribution shifts where even unknown novel classes emerge, the study also explores logical regularization techniques for tasks such as Generalized Category Discovery (GCD), mDG+GCD, and Class Incremental Learning (CIL), proposing a sample-based logical regularization term (L-Reg) to enhance data-, target-, and all-shift generalization. Additionally, a partial logic framework is introduced to address challenges in CIL, enabling models to retain room for unknown classes during training. This is further extended by the Partial-Logic Regularization (PL-Reg), which improves generalization across GCD, mDG+GCD, and transferability for CIL tasks. Furthermore, the thesis proposes a novel Semantic-aware Data Augmentation (SADA) framework for cross-modality generalization in text-to-image synthesis (T2Isyn), text-image retrieval (TIR), and image-text retrieval (ITR) tasks. This framework ensures semantic preservation across text and image modalities, improving both semantic consistency and image quality in cross-modality tasks. The methods proposed in this thesis offer significant advancements in visual generalization and transfer scenarios, providing theoretical insights and practical solutions for handling data shifts, target shifts, and multi-modalities in complex scenarios. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods, demonstrating their superior performance across a range of tasks.

title: Depth of Processing, learner aptitude, and the acquisition of L2 English grammatical structures
authors: Shweta Nigam
abstract: Depth of Processing (DoP) is central to several models of instructed second language acquisition (ISLA) (Leow, 2015). While DoP has been extensively examined in vocabulary learning (e.g., Laufer & Hulstijn, 2001), its role in the acquisition of grammatical structures, particularly through oral and audio-visual modalities remains comparatively underexplored. Drawing on the Levels of Processing framework (Craik & Lockhart, 1972), this study investigated whether task-induced processing depth influences the acquisition of third conditionals and comparatives, and whether language aptitude (LLAMA B, D, F) predicts learning gains. Using a pretest–posttest design, four intact classes involving 108 Grade 8 EFL learners in India were assigned to one of the three experimental conditions differing in level and type of processing: Low DoP, High DoP Explicit, and High DoP Implicit. The treatment task required the participants to listen to an audio-visual story containing the target structures (third conditionals and comparatives) and complete analytic tasks (varying in different groups) before listening to the story for a second time. The oral performance of the participants was analysed for accuracy, and frequency of use of the target structures. A grammaticality judgement test (GJT) and an elicited imitation task (EIT) were used to assess the participants’ gains in the knowledge of the target structures. In addition, language aptitude (LLAMA B, D, F) was measured and modelled as a predictor of gain scores. Results showed a significant effect of processing condition on GJT performance with the High DoP Implicit group outperforming the High DoP Explicit group on total scores and comparatives. In contrast, ANCOVA analyses indicated no significant group differences on EIT outcomes once pretest performance was controlled, with pretest scores strongly predicting posttest performance. In oral production, processing effects were structure-specific: the Low DoP group showed greater accuracy gains for comparatives, while both High DoP groups revealed increased frequency of use of third conditionals. However, across all four measures, multiple regression analyses indicated that LLAMA B, D, and F did not significantly predict gain scores. Overall, the findings support a processing-by-structure pattern: deeper processing benefits were most evident for the more salient structure (comparatives) on an explicit, written measure, whereas complex, low-salience forms (third conditionals) showed limited accuracy change but increased frequency of use under deeper processing.

title: A UAV-Based Framework for Community-Scale Residential Building Energy Modelling in China
authors: Mengfan Jin
abstract: With increasing emphasis on energy efficiency and carbon emission reduction in the building sector, rapid and scalable energy modelling of existing buildings is critical for retrofit projects and policy development. Conventional surveys, data collection and energy modelling processes remain labour-intensive and impractical for large-scale applications, and energy modelling often dominates project time and cost. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) equipped with high-resolution and infrared cameras now offer fast and safe exterior surveys, showing great potential in building energy assessments. Yet, a systematic framework for UAV integration, from image capture through processing to inputs for building energy simulation, has not been established. This research addresses these challenges by developing a structured framework for community-scale building energy modelling, which integrates UAV photogrammetry to accelerate data acquisition, reduce labour, and shorten energy modelling time for retrofit projects. The framework is designed to minimise prior data requirements while maximising automation and retaining sufficient accuracy and reliability. It also addressed systemic issues, such as the lack of data necessary to fully exploit the potential of available technologies in the context of this study. To achieve this research objective, a mixed-methodology approach, combining desk studies and fieldwork, was adopted. First, a comprehensive review of UAV-based building energy studies mapped the current applications and available tools, proposing a preliminary framework. Fieldwork then encompassed a pilot study and a detailed case study. In the pilot test, a single building was surveyed to identify an optimal toolchain for flight planning, image capture, photogrammetric reconstruction, model generation, and selection of a simulation platform. The resulting refined framework was applied to a case study of a 39-building community, and it was demonstrated that further automation was necessary. The potential for automation was then further explored. Geomatic algorithms, machine learning, and deep learning techniques were compared, and the combination that best balanced accuracy and processing time was selected for 3D model generation and window-to-wall ratio (WWR) extraction. In parallel, an archetype library of residential buildings in the Hot Summer Cold Winter (HSCW) zone in China was compiled to facilitate the assignment of thermal parameters. Finally, a reusable community-scale building energy modelling (CBEM) workflow was assembled in Grasshopper using Ladybug Tools components to process the aforementioned inputs. In conclusion, this study integrates UAV photogrammetry, GIS-based geomatic algorithms, machine learning, and graphical programming to develop an UAV-CBEM framework. The outcomes establish a foundation for scalable UAV-based building energy assessments, enhancing applicability in data-limited and large-scale settings worldwide.

title: Spectral Materialism: Encounters with land-time-scapes
authors: Nightingale, Sam
abstract: This transdisciplinary, practice-based PhD introduces spectral materialism through art-based research encounters with ecologically and historically stratified land-time-scapes shaped by hypersalinity and colonial terraforming. Centred in the semi-arid Mallee (southeastern Australia) and read through echoes with California’s Imperial Valley, the project examines how spectral time—the co-presence and haunting of other temporalities—manifests in the material conditions of salt, soil, water, plants, and infrastructures. It asks how learning from geological, First Nations, colonial, and ecological pasts can orient responsibilities in unsettled futures. Treating the present as a crisis of time as much as a crisis of matter, the thesis critiques linear-progressive temporalities bound to Western modernity and extractive regimes. In response, spectral materialism is developed as both a conceptual framework and a critical creative methodology. Through alchemical media experiments with salt crystals, hypersaline soils, and halophytes, photography is reconfigured as a site-responsive, process-oriented practice. Salt is engaged as a material agent and ‘time-crystal’ whose phase shifts—dissolution, saturation, precipitation, crystallisation, evaporation—form a meta-chemistry that refracts deep-marine pasts, settler-colonial irrigation infrastructures, and contemporary dust into processual renderings of time. Methodologically, the project advances attunement as a mode of sensing and responsiveness to forces that are not always immediately perceptible yet are materially active. Field notes appear as para-writing, interrupting linear narration so that heterogeneous times co-present themselves within the text. The thesis is guided by First Nations temporalities—time as relational and in place—while remaining accountable to ethical limits and protocols. The contribution is twofold: a theoretical articulation of spectral materialism as a way to think time otherwise, and a set of site-responsive methods for engaging elemental media in saline environments. Together, they generate materially grounded accounts of spectral presences and open alternative pathways for knowing, sensing, and relating within land-time-scapes marked by enduring colonial and ecological afterlives amid planetary change.

title: DEVELOPMENT AND COMMERCIALIZATION OF COMPUTATIONAL METHODS TO ACCELERATE DERMATOLOGICAL DISCOVERY
authors: Jasson Makkar
abstract: The skin is the largest and outermost organ that surrounds the human body and provides a physical barrier that protects the more delicate internal tissues from the harsh surrounding environment. Over the course of evolution, specialized structures have also arisen in the skin, including sweat and sebaceous glands, nails and claws, and hair follicles. The hair follicle is a multi-lineage mini-organ that is a critical component in defining mammalian species. The gain of function derived from hair and fur benefited these species for millennia due to its insulative and protective properties, mechanosensing function, and ability to serve as camouflage. Current approaches to assess these fibers are generally non-quantitative or are low throughput due to technical limitations of ‘splitting hairs’. We developed a novel deep learning-based computer vision approach for the high throughput quantification of individual hair fibers at a high resolution. Our innovative computer vision tool can distinguish and extract overlapping fibers for quantification of multivariate features including length, width, and color to generate single-hair phenomes (shPhenome) of diverse conditions across the lifespan of mice. Using our tool, we explored the effects of hormone signaling, genetic modifications, and aging on hair follicle output. These analyses revealed novel hair phenotypes as a result of endocrinological, developmental, and aging-related alterations in the fur coats of mice. This tool was then adapted to capture more nuanced hair phenotypes, such as curvature, in a variety of mouse models harboring genetic perturbations. Commercialization of the deep hair phenomics technology presented a unique opportunity to pursue research translation, transforming fundamental biological research into marketable products. Much like the traditional academic route, the path to commercialization requires consistent and continuous iteration, testing of hypotheses, and allowing data to influence and lead subsequent actions. However, as opposed to the pursuit of knowledge, translating research into market-ready solutions requires a focus on consumer needs and the identification of market opportunities. Additionally, the shift in incentive structure requires commercial ventures to prioritize intellectual property protection, alter capital and resource allocation, and seek alternative fundraising sources. The entrepreneurial foundation built through this process culminated in the filing of a provisional patent and establishment of a startup company, kerat Inc. This journey illuminated the multifaceted challenges inherent in closing the gap between academic innovation and commercially viable goods, requiring simultaneous advancement of technical capabilities, adaptation to market dynamics, and fabrication of business infrastructure. Overall, the culmination of work presented in this dissertation sheds light on the importance of quantitatively assessing hair fiber properties to capture the biological phenomena that underlie this fundamental feature of mammalian skin. These findings also highlight the capabilities of this methodology for identifying perturbations in normal growth, potentially indicative of disease or dysfunction. Lastly, this showcased the potential of this technology’s commercial use cases in both the cosmetics and diagnostics industries.
